definition_zh: 占主导地位的；最突出的；占多数的；（生/遗）显性的
definition_en: most common, most powerful, or most noticeable in a place, group, or situation
core_image: 一片森林里同一种树占到七成，其他树种只能从缝隙里看见
scene: 在旧城区的街道上，三层砖房一栋接一栋。Three-storey brick houses are predominant here, and a glass tower appears only once in a whole block.
sceneCN: 这里 predominant 是「占多数的、最显著的」（第 1 个义项：在数量或可见度上占优势）；句意：这里占多数的是三层砖房，一整条街里只偶尔出现一栋玻璃高楼。图中可辨识物件：连排砖房、玻璃高楼、街道、店铺招牌、行道树。

pos.zh: 占主导地位的；最突出的；占多数的

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Most numerous or visible
senses.definition: present in the greatest number or most easily seen
senses.definitionCN: 数量最多或最容易看见
senses.example: Brick houses are predominant in the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 旧城区以砖房为主。
senses.why: The word joins prae- 'before, in front' to dominari 'to rule'. What is predominant stands in front of the rest: it takes the foreground by sheer presence.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把 prae-“在前”与 dominari“统治”连在一起。predominant 之物站在其余之前：它凭存在感占据前景。

senses.title: Having the greatest influence
senses.definition: having more influence or power than others
senses.definitionCN: 影响力或权力超过其他
senses.example: Market forces are the predominant influence on prices.
senses.exampleCN: 市场力量是影响价格的主导因素。
senses.why: Influence is the political half of the word: not how many, but who sets the terms. A view is predominant when the others must answer to it.
senses.whyCN: 影响力是这个词的政治一半：不看数量多少，而看谁定规则。一种观点 predominant，就是其余观点都得回应它。

senses.title: The main characteristic
senses.definition: of a quality, the one that most marks a thing
senses.definitionCN: 在标记某物上最强的性质
senses.example: Her predominant emotion was relief.
senses.exampleCN: 她最主要的情绪是宽慰。
senses.why: Applied to feelings and qualities, the word picks out the note that sounds above the others. It is not the only note, only the loudest.
senses.whyCN: 用于情绪与性质时，这个词挑出盖过其他的那一个音。它不是唯一的音，只是最响的。

senses.title: Dominant in a field
senses.definition: holding the leading position in a field or market
senses.definitionCN: 在某个领域或市场占据领先地位
senses.example: The company is predominant in online retail.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司在网络零售中占主导地位。
senses.why: Business extends the ruling image to market share. Predominance is measured: the leader's share is larger than any rival's, so the metaphor becomes a statistic.
senses.whyCN: 商业把“统治”意象扩展到市场份额。主导地位可以测量：领先者的份额大于任何对手，隐喻于是变成统计数字。

senses.title: The most common species (ecology)
senses.definition: of a species, the most abundant or influential in a community
senses.definitionCN: 群落中数量最多或影响最大的物种
senses.example: Oaks are the predominant trees in this forest.
senses.exampleCN: 橡树是这片森林的优势树种。
senses.why: Ecology counts abundance and cover. A predominant species shapes light, soil, and shelter for the rest, so being numerous turns into being decisive.
senses.whyCN: 生态学计算丰度与盖度。优势种为其余物种决定光照、土壤与庇护，于是“数量多”变成“起决定作用”。

senses.title: The trait that shows (genetics)
senses.definition: of an allele or trait, the one expressed when paired with a recessive one
senses.definitionCN: 与隐性等位基因配对时表现出来的一方
senses.example: Brown eyes are the predominant trait in this family.
senses.exampleCN: 棕眼是这个家族中的显性性状。
senses.why: Genetics borrowed the word for the allele that appears in the phenotype. The expressed trait 'stands in front' while the recessive one stays hidden.
senses.whyCN: 遗传学借这个词指在表型中出现的等位基因。显现的性状“站在前面”，隐性的则藏起来。

senses.title: The leading color or tone
senses.definition: of a color or tone, the one that sets the overall impression
senses.definitionCN: 决定整体印象的那一种颜色或调子
senses.example: Blue is the predominant tone in the painting.
senses.exampleCN: 蓝色是这幅画的主调。
senses.why: In art and design the word describes the ground note of an image. Predominance here is visual weight, not count: a large field of one hue governs the eye.
senses.whyCN: 在艺术与设计中，这个词描述一幅画的底色音。这里的主导是视觉重量而非计数：一大片同色支配眼睛。

senses.title: Ruling or controlling (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, having supreme rule or authority
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：拥有最高统治权或权威
senses.example: The predominant power of the region was the old duchy.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的主导力量是那个老公国。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer, close to dominari 'to rule'. Modern English prefers dominant for political power and keeps predominant for prevalence and prominence.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层，接近 dominari“统治”。现代英语政治上多用 dominant，而 predominant 多指普遍性与突出程度。

intro.en: Predominant came from the language of rule. Its Latin ancestor praedominari means 'to be chief', built from prae- 'before' and dominari 'to rule'. English then softened the political edge into 'most common or most noticeable'.
intro.cn: predominant 出自“统治”的语言。它的拉丁祖先 praedominari 意为“为首”，由 prae-“在前”与 dominari“统治”构成。英语随后把政治锋芒磨成“最常见、最显著”。

items.en: The adjective is first recorded in the sense 'having ascendancy or chief power'.
items.cn: 这个形容词最早记录为“占优势、拥有最高权力”之义。

items.en: From praedominari 'to be chief or predominant', a compound of prae- 'before, in front' and dominari 'to rule'.
items.cn: 来自中世纪拉丁语 praedominari“为首、占主导”，由 prae-“在前”与 dominari“统治”复合。

items.en: dominari comes from dominus 'lord, master', which is built on domus 'house, household'. The lord is the head of the household.
items.cn: dominari 来自 dominus“主人、领主”，后者由 domus“房屋、家户”构成。领主就是家户之首。

items.en: domus is traced to PIE *dem- 'house, household', a reconstruction also behind domestic and domain.
items.cn: domus 被追溯到原始印欧语 *dem-“房屋、家户”，这一重构也见于 domestic 与 domain。

items.en: The sense widens from political power to qualities: a color, a feeling, or a species can be predominant.
items.cn: 义项从政治权力扩展到性质：颜色、情绪或物种都可以是 predominant。

items.en: Modern usage separates the twins: dominant stresses control, predominant stresses prevalence. Statistical and biological writing favor the latter.
items.cn: 现代用法区分这对孪生词：dominant 强调控制，predominant 强调普遍。统计与生物学写作偏用后者。

note.en: The first group is about the same dominus family and spelling; the second is about adjectives that also mean leading or most common.
note.cn: 第一组看同一个 dominus 词族与拼写，第二组看同样表示“领先”或“最常见”的形容词。

entries.definition: to be the strongest or most numerous. It is the verb behind predominant.
entries.definitionCN: 占主导；占多数。它是 predominant 背后的动词。

entries.definition: the state of being predominant. It adds -ance to the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 主导地位；优势。它是动词加 -ance。

entries.definition: controlling or most important. It shares dominari but stresses power rather than prevalence.
entries.definitionCN: 支配的；最重要的。它共享 dominari，但强调权力而非普遍。

entries.definition: existing or happening most often in a place or time. It stresses what currently holds sway.
entries.definitionCN: 在当地或当时最常存在或发生的。它强调当下占上风者。

entries.definition: first in rank or importance. It points to one leading thing, not to a majority.
entries.definitionCN: 等级或重要性第一的。它指一个领先者，而非多数。

entries.definition: found over a large area. It measures reach, not dominance within a group.
entries.definitionCN: 在大范围内可见的。它衡量覆盖范围，而非群体内的支配。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin prae- 'in front' plus dominari 'to rule', the dominant/predominant pair, and the ecology and genetics uses.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 prae-“在前”加 dominari“统治”、dominant 与 predominant 这对词，以及生态学与遗传学用法。

normal.en: Prae- means 'in front'. A predominant thing stands in front of the rest, so the eye and the count both find it first.
normal.cn: prae- 意为“在前”。predominant 之物站在其余之前，所以眼睛与计数都先遇到它。

normal.en: Dominari means 'to rule'. The word began as political power, then learned to describe majorities.
normal.cn: dominari 意为“统治”。这个词从政治权力开始，后来学会描述多数。

normal.en: Dominant vs predominant: dominant controls, predominant prevails. A dominant wolf leads; a predominant tree covers.
normal.cn: dominant 与 predominant：前者控制，后者普遍。dominant 的狼领队，predominant 的树覆盖。

normal.en: In ecology a predominant species is not just numerous; it decides the light and soil for everyone else.
normal.cn: 生态学中，优势种不只是数量多；它为其他所有物种决定光照与土壤。

normal.en: In genetics the predominant allele is the one that shows, standing in front of the hidden recessive one.
normal.cn: 遗传学中，显性等位基因是表现出来的那一个，站在隐藏的隐性基因之前。

abstract.en: Dominance is a relation, not a quantity: something is predominant only against a background of others.
abstract.cn: 支配是一种关系，不是数量：一物只有在其余之物的背景前才成其为主导。

abstract.en: Prevalence hides power: what is most common quietly sets the conditions for everything else.
abstract.cn: 普遍性隐藏着权力：最常见的东西悄悄为其余一切设定条件。

abstract.en: The word lets a color, a gene, and a culture share one grammar: whatever takes the foreground governs the frame.
abstract.cn: 这个词让颜色、基因与文化共享一套语法：占据前景者支配画面。

examples.en: Rice is the predominant crop in the region.
examples.cn: 水稻是该地区的主要作物。

examples.en: The predominant mood was one of cautious optimism.
examples.cn: 主要情绪是谨慎的乐观。

examples.en: Pine trees are predominant on the upper slopes.
examples.cn: 松树在上坡地带占优势。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑来的米能特”——扑过来的米特别多，占了大多数 → predominant 占多数的、主导的

root: 中世纪拉丁语 praedominari“为首”，由 prae-“在前”+ dominari“统治”构成；dominus 源于 domus“家户”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of predominant, all sharing one image: a thing that takes the foreground. The foreground can be counted (majorities), felt (emotions), seen (colors), or inherited (genes).
sensesIntro.cn: predominant 的八个义项共享一个意象：占据前景的东西。这个前景可以被计数（多数）、被感受（情绪）、被看见（颜色）或被遗传（基因）。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one thing standing in front of and above the rest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一物站在其余之前、之上。

branches.en: PRESENCE: sheer numbers and visual weight put one thing in front.
branches.cn: 在场：数量与视觉重量把一物推到前面。

branches.en: INFLUENCE: a view or feeling sets the tone that others must answer to.
branches.cn: 影响：观点或情绪定下其余必须回应的调子。

branches.en: POWER: the old ruling sense survives in markets and in archaic political use.
branches.cn: 权力：古老的统治义在市场中与古旧政治用法里存活。

branches.en: ECOLOGY: abundance becomes decisive when one species shapes the habitat.
branches.cn: 生态：当一个物种塑造栖息地，数量就变成决定力。

branches.en: GENETICS: the expressed allele stands in front while the recessive stays hidden.
branches.cn: 遗传：表达的等位基因站在前面，隐性者藏于其后。

intro.en: Predominant is an adjective built on the verb predominate plus -ant. English adds -ly and -ance, and the base dominari also gives dominant, dominate, and dominion.
intro.cn: predominant 是动词 predominate 加 -ant 构成的形容词。英语加 -ly 与 -ance，词基 dominari 还生成 dominant、dominate、dominion。

latinIntro.en: Latin praedominari 'be chief' combines prae- 'before' with dominari 'rule', from dominus 'lord'. The same dominus family includes dominant, dominion, and domineer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 praedominari“为首”把 prae-“在前”与 dominari“统治”结合，后者出自 dominus“领主”。同一 dominus 词族还有 dominant、dominion、domineer。

definition_zh: 初步的；预备的；前期的；预赛；预备性事项
definition_en: coming before the main part of something, and preparing for it
core_image: 一扇门前的地垫：正式进门之前，先在这里停一下、擦干净鞋
scene: 比赛开始前，裁判先把三十名选手排进同一张名单。The preliminary round cut thirty players down to eight before the main draw began.
sceneCN: 这里 preliminary 是「预赛、预备阶段」（第 3 个义项：正式比赛前的筛选环节）；句意：预赛把三十名选手筛到八名，正赛才开始。图中可辨识物件：赛场、预赛名单、裁判哨、计时器、正赛签表。

pos.zh: 初步的；预备的；前期的
预赛；预备性事项；初步步骤

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Coming before the main part
senses.definition: happening or existing before the main event or part
senses.definitionCN: 在主事件或主体之前发生或存在
senses.example: We held preliminary talks before the summit.
senses.exampleCN: 峰会前我们举行了预备性会谈。
senses.why: The Latin phrase prae limine means 'before the threshold'. A preliminary step is taken at the doorway, before anyone enters the main room.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁短语 prae limine 意为“在门槛之前”。初步步骤是在门口完成的，还没进正厅。

senses.title: Introductory and preparatory
senses.definition: serving to introduce or prepare for something fuller
senses.definitionCN: 用于引出或准备更完整的东西
senses.example: The report begins with a few preliminary remarks.
senses.exampleCN: 报告以几句引言开篇。
senses.why: A preliminary remark prepares the listener's mind the way a vestibule prepares a house: it is part of the building, yet not the room you came for.
senses.whyCN: 引言为听者的心智做准备，如同门厅为房屋做准备：它是建筑的一部分，却不是你要进的那个房间。

senses.title: An early round of a competition
senses.definition: a contest or stage that narrows the field before the final
senses.definitionCN: 在决赛前缩小参赛范围的比赛或阶段
senses.example: She finished first in the preliminary.
senses.exampleCN: 她在预赛中名列第一。
senses.why: Sport borrows the word for its sieve stages. The preliminary exists only to produce the final list, so it is judged by who advances rather than who wins.
senses.whyCN: 体育借这个词来指“筛选阶段”。预赛只为产生决赛名单，所以评判标准是谁晋级，而不是谁夺冠。

senses.title: A preparatory step or arrangement
senses.definition: one of the things done in advance to make a main event possible
senses.definitionCN: 为主要事件铺路而事先完成的事项
senses.example: The preliminaries took longer than the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 准备事项比仪式本身还久。
senses.why: In the plural, the word names the whole backstage: forms, fees, introductions. These steps are usually invisible once the main event begins.
senses.whyCN: 复数形式命名整个后台：表格、费用、介绍。主事件一开始，这些步骤通常就看不见了。

senses.title: Provisional, not final
senses.definition: of a result or finding, based on early evidence and open to change
senses.definitionCN: 结果或发现基于早期证据，仍可能变动
senses.example: Preliminary findings suggest the drug is safe.
senses.exampleCN: 初步结果显示这种药是安全的。
senses.why: Science uses preliminary to mark a claim's status: it is offered for scrutiny, not asserted as settled. The word protects the speaker from the finality of proof.
senses.whyCN: 科学用 preliminary 标记一个主张的地位：它供审视，而非断言已定。这个词保护说话者，使其不必承担“已证”的终局。

senses.title: A qualifying heat in sport
senses.definition: a race or match that decides who enters the main competition
senses.definitionCN: 决定谁进入主赛的预跑或预赛
senses.example: He ran a personal best in the preliminaries.
senses.exampleCN: 他在预赛中跑出个人最好成绩。
senses.why: The heat is a filter, not a show. Preliminary times only select; medals are awarded later, which is why records set in heats can feel strangely weightless.
senses.whyCN: 预赛是筛子，不是演出。预赛成绩只作选拔；奖牌在后面发，所以预赛里创的纪录会有一种奇特的失重感。

senses.title: A hearing held before trial
senses.definition: a court session that decides whether a case should go to trial
senses.definitionCN: 决定案件是否进入正式审判的法庭程序
senses.example: The judge set a preliminary hearing for next month.
senses.exampleCN: 法官把预审定在下个月。
senses.why: Law needs a gate before the trial: the preliminary hearing tests whether there is enough evidence. The threshold image becomes a procedural safeguard.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要审判前的一道门：预审检验证据是否足够。门槛意象变成程序保障。

senses.title: An introductory statement or section
senses.definition: a short opening text that prepares the reader
senses.definitionCN: 为读者做准备的简短开篇文字
senses.example: The book opens with a preliminary on method.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书以一篇方法引言开篇。
senses.why: In scholarship, preliminaries include prefaces and front matter. They frame the main text the way a prologue frames a play: outside the action, yet necessary to it.
senses.whyCN: 在学术写作中，preliminaries 包括序言与卷首材料。它们框住正文，如同开场白框住戏剧：在情节之外，却不可或缺。

intro.en: Preliminary is a threshold word. Its Latin source is the phrase prae limine, 'before the threshold', and every sense keeps that image: something done at the door before entering.
intro.cn: preliminary 是一个关于门槛的词。它的拉丁来源是短语 prae limine“在门槛之前”，每个义项都保留这个意象：进门之前先在门口完成的事。

items.en: First recorded as an adjective meaning 'introductory, preparatory'.
items.cn: 最早记录为形容词，义为“引言的、预备的”。

items.en: From Latin prae limine 'before the threshold', from prae- 'before' and limen 'threshold, door'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁短语 prae limine“在门槛之前”，由 prae-“在前”与 limen“门槛、门”构成。

items.en: limen is the same noun behind eliminate and subliminal. A threshold is both a physical edge and the limit of what can be perceived.
items.cn: limen 也是 eliminate 与 subliminal 背后的名词。门槛既是物理边缘，也是感知的界限。

items.en: The noun use for preparatory steps and early rounds develops in the 18c.–19c., often in the plural.
items.cn: 指预备步骤与早期轮次的名词用法在 18–19 世纪发展起来，常用复数。

items.en: Modern English uses the adjective for provisional findings and the noun for sporting and legal gates.
items.cn: 现代英语用形容词指暂定结论，用名词指体育与法律中的“关口”。

note.en: The first group shares the limen or preliminary stem; the second is about words that also mean coming first or preparing the way.
note.cn: 第一组共享 limen 词干或 preliminary 的构词，第二组看同样表示“在先”或“铺路”的词。

entries.definition: a preliminary exam or round, used informally. It is a clipped form.
entries.definitionCN: 预考或预赛，非正式缩略。

entries.definition: preliminary exams or front matter in a book.
entries.definitionCN: 初试；书籍卷首材料。

entries.definition: below the threshold of consciousness. It uses the same Latin limen.
entries.definitionCN: 阈下的；意识界限以下的。它用同一个拉丁词 limen。

entries.definition: serving as an introduction. It names the function, not the threshold image.
entries.definitionCN: 用作引言的。它命名功能，而非门槛意象。

entries.definition: arranged for the present and liable to change. It fits preliminary findings but not early rounds.
entries.definitionCN: 暂时安排、可变的。它贴合“初步结果”，不贴合“预赛”。

entries.definition: done to get ready for something. It stresses readiness rather than position.
entries.definitionCN: 为某事做准备的。它强调准备状态，而非位置。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin limen 'threshold', the phrase prae limine, the sporting and legal gate uses, and the adjective/noun pair.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 limen“门槛”、短语 prae limine、体育与法律中的“关口”用法，以及形容词与名词两种词性。

normal.en: Prae limine means 'before the threshold'. Everything preliminary happens at the door, before the main room.
normal.cn: prae limine 意为“在门槛之前”。一切 preliminary 的事都发生在门口，还没进正厅。

normal.en: Limen is also in eliminate and subliminal: a threshold can be a physical edge or a limit of perception.
normal.cn: limen 也见于 eliminate 与 subliminal：门槛可以是物理边缘，也可以是感知界限。

normal.en: A preliminary round is a sieve: it exists to produce the final list, not to award the prize.
normal.cn: 预赛是一张筛子：它的存在是为了产生决赛名单，而不是发奖。

normal.en: Preliminary findings are offered for scrutiny, not asserted as settled. The word marks a claim as open.
normal.cn: 初步结果供审视，而非断言已定。这个词把主张标记为“未关”。

normal.en: The noun usually appears in the plural: the preliminaries are the backstage steps nobody watches.
normal.cn: 名词通常用复数：preliminaries 是没人观看的后台步骤。

abstract.en: Every entrance has a threshold, and every threshold has a rule: what must be left outside before you may come in.
abstract.cn: 每道入口都有门槛，每道门槛都有规则：进门之前必须把什么留在外面。

abstract.en: The preliminary is powerful because it decides who gets to be judged at all.
abstract.cn: 预赛之所以有力，是因为它决定谁才有资格被评判。

abstract.en: Calling a result preliminary is an act of intellectual honesty: it keeps the door open instead of sealing the room.
abstract.cn: 把结果称作“初步”，是一种智识上的诚实：它让门继续开着，而不是封死房间。

examples.en: The preliminary results look promising.
examples.cn: 初步结果看起来有希望。

examples.en: She was eliminated in the preliminary round.
examples.cn: 她在预赛轮被淘汰。

examples.en: These talks are preliminary to a formal agreement.
examples.cn: 这些会谈是正式协议的前奏。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of preliminary, all set at the threshold. The word can describe a step (talks, remarks), a stage (a heat, a hearing), or a status (findings still open to change).
sensesIntro.cn: preliminary 的八个义项都发生在门槛处。这个词可以描述一个步骤（会谈、引言）、一个阶段（预赛、预审），或一种状态（仍可变动的研究结果）。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: standing at the threshold before entering the main room.
core.cn: 核心意象：进入正厅之前，站在门槛上。

branches.en: THRESHOLD: remarks and front matter stand outside the main text yet belong to it.
branches.cn: 门槛：引言与卷首材料站在正文之外，却属于它。

branches.en: PREPARE: the backstage steps make the main event possible.
branches.cn: 准备：后台步骤使主事件成为可能。

branches.en: QUALIFY: an early round filters the field before the final.
branches.cn: 选拔：早期轮次在决赛前筛出参赛者。

branches.en: PROVISIONAL: a finding marked preliminary is still open to revision.
branches.cn: 暂定：标记为初步的结论仍可修改。

branches.en: LEGAL GATE: a hearing tests whether a case may enter trial.
branches.cn: 法律关口：预审检验案件能否进入审判。

intro.en: Preliminary is an adjective that also works as a noun. English adds -ly and clips it to prelim, while the Latin limen also builds eliminate and subliminal.
intro.cn: preliminary 是可作名词的形容词。英语加 -ly，并缩略为 prelim；拉丁语 limen 还构成 eliminate 与 subliminal。

latinIntro.en: The Latin phrase prae limine 'before the threshold' yields preliminary and, through limen, eliminate and subliminal. The threshold is both a doorway and a limit.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁短语 prae limine“在门槛之前”生成 preliminary，并经 limen 生成 eliminate 与 subliminal。门槛既是门口，也是界限。

definition_zh: 假定；推测；擅自；胆敢；（法律）推定
definition_en: to suppose something is true without proof, or to dare to do something without permission
core_image: 还没进门就先假定门里的灯是亮的，抬脚就走
scene: 电话一直没人接。Because no one answered the phone, she could only presume that her friend was already on the way, so she went straight to the station to wait.
sceneCN: 这里 presume 是「假定、推测」（第 1 个义项：在没有证据时先认定某事为真）；句意：因为没人接电话，她只能假定朋友已经在路上，于是直接去车站等。图中可辨识物件：无人接听的电话、时刻表、车站长椅、行李箱、手表。

pos.zh: 假定；推测；擅自；胆敢
假定；放肆（presume on）

senses.title: Suppose without proof
senses.definition: to believe something is true before there is proof
senses.definitionCN: 在证据之前就相信某事为真
senses.example: I presume you have read the report.
senses.exampleCN: 我想你已经读过报告了。
senses.why: Latin praesumere means 'take before': prae- 'before' plus sumere 'take'. The mind takes a proposition as a starting point rather than waiting for evidence.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praesumere 意为“先取”：prae-“在前”加 sumere“取”。心智把某个命题先拿来做起点，而不等证据。

senses.title: Take for granted
senses.definition: to accept something as true without checking it
senses.definitionCN: 不加核对就接受某事为真
senses.example: We presume the train will be on time.
senses.exampleCN: 我们想当然地认为火车会准点。
senses.why: The everyday sense is a habit of the mind: what is normally true is taken as true again. Presumption is assumption made comfortable by repetition.
senses.whyCN: 日常义是一种心智习惯：通常为真的事，就再当作真。推定是被重复养得舒服的假定。

senses.title: Assume legally (presumed innocent)
senses.definition: in law, to treat a fact as established until disproved
senses.definitionCN: 法律中，在未被反驳前把某事实视为成立
senses.example: A defendant is presumed innocent until proved guilty.
senses.exampleCN: 被告在被证明有罪前被推定无罪。
senses.why: Legal systems must act before certainty. Presumption supplies a default that can be attacked by evidence, so the burden of proof is allocated by the word.
senses.whyCN: 法律系统必须在确定之前行动。推定提供一个可被证据攻击的默认值，于是证明责任由这个词来分配。

senses.title: Dare to do something
senses.definition: to venture to do something that may be unwelcome or beyond your right
senses.definitionCN: 贸然做可能不受欢迎或越权的事
senses.example: I would not presume to tell you your job.
senses.exampleCN: 我不敢冒昧指点你的工作。
senses.why: The 'take before' image turns social: to presume is to take a step before permission is given. The act is not illegal, only ahead of its warrant.
senses.whyCN: “先取”意象转向社会：presume 是在许可之前先迈一步。这行为不违法，只是走在了授权之前。

senses.title: Be presumptuous or overbold
senses.definition: to behave with more confidence or freedom than is proper
senses.definitionCN: 以超出分寸的自信或自由行事
senses.example: He presumed too far with his host's kindness.
senses.exampleCN: 他过于利用主人的好意了。
senses.why: When the object is another person's goodwill, 'taking before' becomes taking advantage. The adjective presumptuous names this excess directly.
senses.whyCN: 当对象是他人的善意，“先取”就变成占便宜。形容词 presumptuous 直接命名这种越界。

senses.title: Take advantage of (presume on)
senses.definition: to rely too much on someone's tolerance or generosity
senses.definitionCN: 过度依赖某人的宽容或慷慨
senses.example: She presumed on their hospitality and stayed a month.
senses.exampleCN: 她仗着他们的好客住了一个月。
senses.why: The phrasal verb marks the target of the taking: what is presumed upon is the patience of another. The word records a debt that was never asked for.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语动词标出“取”的对象：被 presume upon 的是他人的耐心。这个词记录了一笔从未被同意的亏欠。

senses.title: Suppose as a working hypothesis
senses.definition: to adopt a proposition provisionally in order to reason from it
senses.definitionCN: 为推理而暂时采用一个命题
senses.example: Presume the data are accurate and see what follows.
senses.exampleCN: 假定数据准确，看看会推出什么。
senses.why: In logic and science a presumption is a deliberate starting point. The word asks the listener to grant it for the sake of the argument, not to believe it outright.
senses.whyCN: 在逻辑与科学中，presumption 是刻意的起点。这个词请听者为了论证暂时承认它，而不是彻底相信它。

senses.title: Presume death after absence
senses.definition: in law, to declare a missing person dead after a set period
senses.definitionCN: 法律中，在特定期限后宣告失踪者死亡
senses.example: The court presumed him dead after seven years.
senses.exampleCN: 七年后法庭推定他已死亡。
senses.why: This is presumption at its most literal: the law cannot see the person, so it takes the most probable fact and acts on it. The missing body is replaced by a legal certainty.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的推定：法律看不见那个人，于是取最可能的事实并据此行动。失踪的身体被一个法律确定性取代。

senses.title: Believe on probability
senses.definition: to hold a belief because it is likely, not because it is proved
senses.definitionCN: 因某事很可能而相信，而非因已证明
senses.example: We presume the cause was a short circuit.
senses.exampleCN: 我们推测原因是短路。
senses.why: The word's epistemic core: belief proportioned to likelihood. It sits between guess (weak) and know (strong), and usually signals that the speaker is aware of the gap.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词的认识论核心：与可能性相称的相信。它位于 guess（弱）与 know（强）之间，通常表示说话者意识到那道缺口。

intro.en: Presume is built from 'take before': prae- 'before' plus sumere 'to take'. It differs from assume, which is 'take to oneself'. The legal and social senses grow from that single gesture of taking ahead of proof or permission.
intro.cn: presume 由“先取”构成：prae-“在前”加 sumere“取”。它与 assume（“取到自己身上”）不同。法律义与社会义都从这一个“在证据或许可之前先取”的动作生长出来。

items.en: First recorded with the sense 'take upon oneself, venture, dare'.
items.cn: 最早记录为“承担、冒险、胆敢”之义。

items.en: From Latin praesumere 'take before, take for granted, anticipate' = prae- 'before' + sumere 'take up'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 praesumere“先取、视为当然、预料”= prae-“在前”+ sumere“取起”。

items.en: sumere is sub- 'under' + emere 'take, buy', the verb behind assume, consume, resume, and sumption. Presume takes before; assume takes to oneself.
items.cn: sumere 是 sub-“在下”+ emere“取、买”，也是 assume、consume、resume、sumption 的动词。presume 是先取，assume 是取到自己身上。

items.en: The legal sense 'take as established until disproved' develops, giving presumption and presumptive.
items.cn: 法律义“在未被反驳前视为成立”发展出来，产生 presumption 与 presumptive。

items.en: The negative social sense 'overbold, taking too much upon oneself' produces presumptuous.
items.cn: 负面的社会义“过分大胆、越权”产生 presumptuous。

items.en: Modern English keeps both faces: an epistemic default and a social trespass. Presumably marks the first; presumptuous marks the second.
items.cn: 现代英语保留两副面孔：认识上的默认与社会上的越界。presumably 标记前者，presumptuous 标记后者。

note.en: The first group shares the sumere root and the -sume spelling; the second is about verbs that also mean supposing or daring.
note.cn: 第一组共享 sumere 词根与 -sume 拼写，第二组看同样表示“假定”或“胆敢”的动词。

entries.definition: to take as true, or to take power. It uses ad- 'to' + sumere, taking to oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 假定；承担；夺取。它用 ad-“向”+ sumere，取到自己身上。

entries.definition: to begin again after a pause. It is re- 'again' + sumere.
entries.definitionCN: 暂停后再开始。它是 re-“再”+ sumere。

entries.definition: a belief taken for granted, or boldness. It is presume plus -tion.
entries.definitionCN: 想当然的信念；放肆。它是 presume 加 -tion。

entries.definition: to think something is probably true. It is softer and more conversational than presume.
entries.definitionCN: 认为某事可能为真。它比 presume 更软、更口语。

entries.definition: to take something as true without proof. It lacks presume's note of daring or legal weight.
entries.definitionCN: 未经证明即视为真。它没有 presume 的“胆敢”或法律分量。

entries.definition: to be brave enough to do something. It names courage, while presume names overstepping.
entries.definitionCN: 勇敢到敢做某事。它命名勇气，presume 命名越界。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin prae- 'before' plus sumere 'take', the presume/assume pair, legal presumption, and the phrase presume on someone.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 prae-“在前”加 sumere“取”、presume 与 assume 这对词、法律推定，以及 presume on someone 这一搭配。

normal.en: Prae- means 'before' and sumere means 'take': presume is to take a belief before you have proof.
normal.cn: prae- 意为“在前”，sumere 意为“取”：presume 就是在有证据之前先取一个信念。

normal.en: Assume is ad- plus sumere, 'take to yourself'; presume is prae- plus sumere, 'take beforehand'. The prefixes tell the difference.
normal.cn: assume 是 ad- 加 sumere，“取到自己身上”；presume 是 prae- 加 sumere，“先取”。前缀说明差别。

normal.en: In law, presumption is a default the other side must attack: presumed innocent until proved guilty.
normal.cn: 法律中，presumption 是一个对方必须攻击的默认值：在被证明有罪前推定无罪。

normal.en: Presume on someone is to take their patience before asking: the debt is real even if no one agreed to it.
normal.cn: presume on someone 是在开口前就先取用对方的耐心：即使没人同意，这笔亏欠也真实存在。

normal.en: Presumably is the everyday adverb: it marks what the speaker thinks is likely but cannot prove.
normal.cn: presumably 是日常副词：标记说话者认为很可能却无法证明的事。

abstract.en: All action starts before certainty: presumption is the credit we extend to the world so that we can move.
abstract.cn: 一切行动都始于确定之前：推定是我们给世界的一笔信用，好让自己能动起来。

abstract.en: The same gesture that lets thought begin can become a social trespass: taking an idea early and taking a person's goodwill early are cousins.
abstract.cn: 让思想得以开始的动作，也可能变成社会越界：提前拿走一个观念，和提前取用一个人的善意，是表亲。

abstract.en: Presumption distributes the burden of proof: whoever presumes forces the other to speak.
abstract.cn: 推定分配证明责任：谁作出推定，谁就迫使对方开口。

examples.en: I presume you have already booked the tickets.
examples.cn: 我想你已经订好票了。

examples.en: The defendant is presumed innocent until proven guilty.
examples.cn: 被告在被证明有罪前被推定无罪。

examples.en: He presumed on her patience once too often.
examples.cn: 他仗着她的耐心，终于越过了头。

root: 拉丁语 praesumere“先取”，由 prae-“在前”+ sumere“取”构成；sumere = sub- + emere“取”。与 assume（ad- + sumere）区分。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of presume, all one gesture: taking before. The mind takes a belief before proof; a person takes a step before permission; the law takes a fact before certainty.
sensesIntro.cn: presume 的九个义项，都是同一个动作：先取。心智在证据前取一个信念；人在许可前先迈一步；法律在确定前取一个事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: taking something before you are entitled to it.
core.cn: 核心意象：在你尚未获得资格之前就先拿走。

branches.en: SUPPOSE: the mind takes a proposition early and reasons from it.
branches.cn: 假定：心智提前取一个命题并从中推理。

branches.en: HABIT: what is usually true is taken as true again without checking.
branches.cn: 习惯：通常为真的事不再核对就被当作真。

branches.en: LEGAL: the law adopts a default fact so it can act before certainty.
branches.cn: 法律：法律采用默认事实，以便在确定之前行动。

branches.en: DARE: to presume is to act before permission, and the excess has its own adjective.
branches.cn: 胆敢：presume 是在许可前行动，这种越界有专属形容词。

branches.en: EXPLOIT: presuming on a person turns taking-before into taking advantage.
branches.cn: 利用：presume on 某人，把“先取”变成占便宜。

intro.en: Presume is a Latin verb. English adds -tion, -tuous, -tive, and -ably, and the root sumere also builds assume, consume, and resume.
intro.cn: presume 是拉丁动词。英语加 -tion、-tuous、-tive、-ably，词根 sumere 还构成 assume、consume、resume。

latinIntro.en: Latin praesumere 'take before' sits beside assumere 'take to oneself' and sumere 'take up'. The prefix decides the meaning, which is why presume and assume are not interchangeable.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 praesumere“先取”旁边是 assumere“取到自己身上”与 sumere“取起”。前缀决定含义，所以 presume 与 assume 不可互换。

definition_zh: 以前的；先前的；上一个的；以前的（所有者等）
definition_en: existing or happening before something else, especially immediately before
core_image: 一条路上留下的一串脚印：你已经走过的那一段
scene: 会议开始前，主持人先翻开旧纪要。The chair read the minutes of the previous meeting first, so that everyone remembered what had been decided last time.
sceneCN: 这里 previous 是「上一次的、先前的」（第 2 个义项：紧接在这一次之前的那一次）；句意：主持人先读了上一次会议的纪要，让大家记起上次决定了什么。图中可辨识物件：会议桌、旧纪要、日历、文件夹、投影幕。

pos.zh: 以前的；先前的；上一个的

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Happening before in time
senses.definition: existing or occurring earlier than something else
senses.definitionCN: 比另一事物更早存在或发生
senses.example: Previous studies reached a different conclusion.
senses.exampleCN: 先前的研究得出了不同结论。
senses.why: Latin praevius means 'going before', from prae- 'before' and via 'way'. The word pictures something that has already travelled the road you are now on.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praevius 意为“走在前面的”，由 prae-“在前”与 via“道路”构成。这个词描绘已经走完你脚下这段路的东西。

senses.title: Immediately preceding
senses.definition: the one directly before the current one
senses.definitionCN: 紧挨着当前这个之前的那个
senses.example: The previous chapter explained the method.
senses.exampleCN: 上一章解释了方法。
senses.why: English often uses the word for the nearest predecessor, not any earlier item. The road image narrows to the step just behind your heel.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用它指最近的前一个，而非任何更早的项。道路意象收窄到脚跟后的那一步。

senses.title: Former, no longer current
senses.definition: holding a position or relationship no longer held
senses.definitionCN: 担任的职位或关系已不再持续
senses.example: The previous owner kept the garden beautiful.
senses.exampleCN: 前任主人把花园打理得很美。
senses.why: When attached to a role or person, the word marks a slot that has changed hands. What is previous is not merely earlier but replaced.
senses.whyCN: 当它附着于角色或人时，标记一个已经易手的槽位。previous 不只是更早，而是已被取代。

senses.title: Earlier in a sequence or order
senses.definition: coming earlier in an ordered series
senses.definitionCN: 在有序序列中更早出现
senses.example: Check the previous entry in the log.
senses.exampleCN: 检查日志中的前一条。
senses.why: Sequences let 'before' be counted: the previous item is the one at index n-1. The spatial image of the road becomes an ordered list.
senses.whyCN: 序列让“在前”可以计数：previous 项就是索引 n-1 的那一项。道路的空间意象变成有序列表。

senses.title: Before, in the phrase previous to
senses.definition: in formal usage, earlier than or before
senses.definitionCN: 正式用法：早于、在……之前
senses.example: Previous to 1900, the town had no railway.
senses.exampleCN: 1900 年以前，这个镇没有铁路。
senses.why: The phrase turns the adjective into a preposition. It is more formal than 'before' and slightly archaic in speech, but common in legal and historical writing.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把形容词变成介词。它比 before 正式，口语中略古旧，但在法律与历史写作中常见。

senses.title: Premature or hasty (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, happening too soon, before the proper time
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：发生得过早，早于适当时间
senses.example: a previous conclusion, drawn before the evidence
senses.exampleCN: 证据未齐就作出的过早结论
senses.why: The word once carried the sense 'too early', not only 'earlier'. The Latin comparative idea of going ahead could imply jumping the gun.
senses.whyCN: 这个词曾有“过早”而非仅仅“更早”的意思。拉丁语“走在前面”的比较意味，可以暗指抢跑。

senses.title: The antecedent term (logic)
senses.definition: in logic, the premise or term that comes before another
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑中先于另一项的前提或词项
senses.example: The previous proposition must be established first.
senses.exampleCN: 前一个命题必须先被确立。
senses.why: Logic orders propositions in a chain. The previous proposition is the ground on which the next stands, so priority becomes inference.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑把命题排成链。前一个命题是后一个站立的地面，于是“在先”变成推理关系。

senses.title: Already mentioned or known
senses.definition: already referred to earlier in a text or conversation
senses.definitionCN: 在文本或谈话中已被提及
senses.example: The previous example shows the pattern clearly.
senses.exampleCN: 前面的例子清楚展示了这个模式。
senses.why: Reference needs a backward pointer. The word tells the reader to look up the road already travelled, which is why it is so common in academic prose.
senses.whyCN: 指称需要一个向后指的箭头。这个词让读者回望已经走过的路，所以它在学术写作中如此常见。

intro.en: Previous is a road word: Latin praevius 'going before' combines prae- 'before' with via 'way'. English borrowed it in the 17c. and made it the ordinary adjective for the step just behind.
intro.cn: previous 是一个道路词：拉丁语 praevius“走在前面的”把 prae-“在前”与 via“道路”结合。英语在 17 世纪借入，并让它成为指“刚过去那一步”的常用形容词。

items.en: The adjective is first recorded in English with the sense 'going before in time or order'.
items.cn: 这个形容词最早在英语中记录为“在时间或次序上在前”之义。

items.en: From Latin praevius 'leading the way, going before' = prae- 'before' + via 'way, road'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 praevius“引路、走在前”= prae-“在前”+ via“道路”。

items.en: via also yields deviate, obvious, trivial, convey, and voyage. The family is about roads, and 'before on the road' is the core of previous.
items.cn: via 还生成 deviate、obvious、trivial、convey、voyage。这个词族关乎道路，而“路上在前”正是 previous 的核心。

items.en: The word settles into its modern sense, especially 'the one immediately before'.
items.cn: 这个词稳定在现代义，尤其指“紧接在前的那一个”。

items.en: The prepositional phrase previous to becomes common in formal prose in the 18c.
items.cn: 介词短语 previous to 在 18 世纪正式书面语中变得常见。

items.en: Modern English prefers before in speech and keeps previous to for legal and historical writing.
items.cn: 现代英语口语偏好 before，法律与历史写作保留 previous to。

note.en: The first group shares the via or -vious shape; the second is about adjectives that also mean earlier.
note.cn: 第一组共享 via 或 -vious 的形态，第二组看同样表示“更早”的形容词。

entries.definition: at an earlier time. It is previous plus -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 以前；先前。它是 previous 加 -ly。

entries.definition: clear, literally 'in the way'. It uses the same via.
entries.definitionCN: 明显的，字面“挡在路上”。它用同一个 via。

entries.definition: to go off the way. It is de- 'away from' + via.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离道路。它是 de-“离开”+ via。

entries.definition: earlier or more important. It is stronger and more formal than previous.
entries.definitionCN: 更早或更重要的。它比 previous 更强、更正式。

entries.definition: the earlier of two, or a past holder of a role. It contrasts with 'latter'.
entries.definitionCN: 两者中在前的，或某角色的前任。它与 latter 相对。

entries.definition: coming just before in order. It is the precise word for the item at n-1.
entries.definitionCN: 在次序上紧接其前。它是指 n-1 项的确切词。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin via 'road', the praevius image of going before, the previous/prior/former trio, and the phrase previous to.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 via“道路”、praevius“走在前面”的意象、previous/prior/former 三词的区别，以及短语 previous to。

normal.en: Via means 'road'. Previous things have already walked the road you are on.
normal.cn: via 意为“道路”。previous 的东西已经走过你脚下的路。

normal.en: Prae- means 'before'. Put the two together and you get 'going before on the way'.
normal.cn: prae- 意为“在前”。两者相加就是“在路上走在前面”。

normal.en: Previous vs prior: previous is the everyday 'last one'; prior is formal and can also mean 'more important'.
normal.cn: previous 与 prior：previous 是日常的“上一个”，prior 更正式，还可表示“更重要”。

normal.en: Previous vs former: former contrasts with latter in a pair; previous can point to any earlier item.
normal.cn: previous 与 former：former 在一对中与 latter 相对；previous 可指任何更早的项。

normal.en: Previous to is a formal preposition: lawyers and historians use it, everyday speech says before.
normal.cn: previous to 是正式介词：律师与历史学家用它，日常口语说 before。

abstract.en: Memory is the road behind us: to call something previous is to locate it on that road, not merely to date it.
abstract.cn: 记忆是我们身后的路：称某物 previous，就是把它定位在那条路上，而不只是给它标日期。

abstract.en: Every present moment defines its predecessor, so 'previous' is a relational word disguised as a time word.
abstract.cn: 每个当下都在定义它的前一刻，所以 previous 是一个伪装成时间词的关系词。

abstract.en: The past is not one thing: previous, former, and prior cut it differently, by nearness, role, and rank.
abstract.cn: 过去不是一整块：previous、former、prior 按近远、角色与等级把它切成不同的段。

examples.en: The previous meeting lasted three hours.
examples.cn: 上一次会议开了三个小时。

examples.en: She had no previous experience in teaching.
examples.cn: 她此前没有教学经验。

examples.en: Previous to that year, the village had no school.
examples.cn: 在那一年之前，这个村子没有学校。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑瑞威士”——扑向前一个瑞威士（路标）→ previous 先前的、上一个

root: 拉丁语 praevius“走在前面的”，由 prae-“在前”+ via“道路”构成；同族有 deviate、obvious、trivial、convey。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of previous, all placed on a road behind the present. The road can be time (last year), a list (the item before), a role (the former owner), or a text (the example above).
sensesIntro.cn: previous 的八个义项都放在当下身后的一条路上。这条路可以是时间（去年）、列表（前一项）、角色（前任）或文本（上面的例子）。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the stretch of road already walked.
core.cn: 核心意象：已经走过的那一段路。

branches.en: BEFORE: earlier in time, with an archaic note of 'too early'.
branches.cn: 在前：时间上更早，古义带“过早”色彩。

branches.en: JUST BEFORE: the nearest predecessor in a sequence or list.
branches.cn: 紧邻在前：序列或列表中最近的前一项。

branches.en: FORMER: a role or owner that has been replaced.
branches.cn: 前任：已被取代的角色或所有者。

branches.en: PREPOSITION: previous to turns the adjective into a formal 'before'.
branches.cn: 介词：previous to 把形容词变成正式的“在……之前”。

branches.en: REFERENCE: in logic and texts, the earlier item grounds or points back.
branches.cn: 指称：在逻辑与文本中，前项提供依据或向后指。

intro.en: Previous is an adjective from Latin praevius. English adds -ly and -ness, and the same via builds deviate, obvious, and convey.
intro.cn: previous 是来自拉丁 praevius 的形容词。英语加 -ly 与 -ness，同一个 via 还构成 deviate、obvious、convey。

latinIntro.en: Latin praevius 'going before' combines prae- 'before' with via 'way'. The via family is large: deviate, obvious, trivial, convey, voyage. All keep the image of a road.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 praevius“走在前”把 prae-“在前”与 via“道路”结合。via 词族很大：deviate、obvious、trivial、convey、voyage。它们都保留道路意象。

definition_zh: 主要的；首要的；最初的；初级的；原生的；（美国）初选
definition_en: first in importance, order, or development; basic rather than derived
core_image: 一排门中最先打开的那一扇，所有人从这里进入
scene: 急救现场，医生先检查呼吸、出血与意识。Her primary check covered breathing, bleeding and awareness, and everything else waited until those three were answered.
sceneCN: 这里 primary 是「首要的、第一位的」（第 1 个义项：在重要性上排第一）；句意：她的首要检查覆盖呼吸、出血和意识，其余项目都等这三项有答案之后才做。图中可辨识物件：急救包、担架、监护仪、手电筒、评估表。

pos.zh: 主要的；首要的；最初的；初级的；原生的
初选；初级选举；（鸟）初级飞羽

senses.title: First in importance
senses.definition: more important than all others
senses.definitionCN: 比其余一切更重要
senses.example: Safety is our primary concern.
senses.exampleCN: 安全是我们的首要关切。
senses.why: Latin primarius means 'of the first rank'. The word ranks things: one item is placed in the first position, and the others are measured against it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 primarius 意为“第一等的”。这个词给事物排名：一项被放到第一位，其余都以它为参照。

senses.title: First in order or time
senses.definition: coming first in a sequence or process
senses.definitionCN: 在序列或过程中最先出现
senses.example: The primary stage of the reaction takes seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 反应的初始阶段只需几秒。
senses.why: Order and importance borrow the same image. What comes first in time is often what must be dealt with first, so sequence slides into priority.
senses.whyCN: 次序与重要性借用同一意象。时间上最先的，往往也是必须先处理的，于是序列滑向优先。

senses.title: Basic or elementary
senses.definition: of the first level of education or skill
senses.definitionCN: 教育或技能的第一层
senses.example: Children learn to read in primary school.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在小学学习阅读。
senses.why: Primary education is the first tier, before secondary. The word names a floor of a building rather than a value judgment.
senses.whyCN: 初等教育是第二级之前的第一层。这个词命名建筑的一层楼，而非价值判断。

senses.title: Chief or main
senses.definition: the main or principal part of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物的主要或主体部分
senses.example: The primary cause was a failed valve.
senses.exampleCN: 主要原因是阀门失效。
senses.why: Here primary is close to principal: it picks out the leading element in an explanation. The two words share a root but differ in role.
senses.whyCN: 这里 primary 接近 principal：它挑出解释中的主导要素。两词共享词根，但角色不同。

senses.title: Original, not derived
senses.definition: of a source or record, created at the time, not based on another
senses.definitionCN: 来源或记录在当时产生，而非依据他物
senses.example: Historians prefer primary sources such as letters.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家偏爱书信这类原始资料。
senses.why: Research divides evidence into first-hand and second-hand. A primary source is the earliest layer; everything else is commentary on it.
senses.whyCN: 研究把证据分为第一手与第二手。原始资料是最早的一层，其余都是对它的评论。

senses.title: A US primary election
senses.definition: a state election in which voters choose party candidates
senses.definitionCN: 选民在其中选出政党候选人的州级选举
senses.example: She won the New Hampshire primary.
senses.exampleCN: 她赢下了新罕布什尔州初选。
senses.why: American politics uses the noun for the first screening election in a campaign. The word keeps its 'first stage' sense: the primary precedes the general election.
senses.whyCN: 美国政治用这个名词指竞选中的第一场筛选性选举。它保留“第一阶段”义：初选在普选之前。

senses.title: A primary feather
senses.definition: one of the flight feathers on the outer part of a bird's wing
senses.definitionCN: 鸟翼外侧的飞行羽毛
senses.example: The hawk's primaries spread wide in flight.
senses.exampleCN: 猎鹰飞行时初级飞羽大张。
senses.why: Ornithology numbers feathers from the leading edge outward. The primaries are the first flight feathers, so the word's ordinal sense becomes anatomy.
senses.whyCN: 鸟类学从翼前缘向外编号。初级飞羽是最先的飞行羽毛，于是序数义变成解剖名。

senses.title: First in a chemical chain
senses.definition: of a carbon atom or compound, attached to one other carbon group
senses.definitionCN: 碳原子或化合物只与一个其他碳基相连
senses.example: Primary alcohols oxidize to aldehydes.
senses.exampleCN: 伯醇氧化成醛。
senses.why: Chemistry labels structures by position in a chain: primary, secondary, tertiary. The naming is ordinal, borrowed straight from the Latin 'first rank'.
senses.whyCN: 化学按链上的位置标记结构：伯、仲、叔。命名是序数性的，直接借自拉丁语“第一等”。

senses.title: One of the primary colors
senses.definition: in color theory, a color from which others can be mixed
senses.definitionCN: 色彩理论中可混合出其他颜色的基色
senses.example: Red, blue, and yellow are primary colors in painting.
senses.exampleCN: 在绘画中，红、蓝、黄是三原色。
senses.why: Color theory treats some hues as underived: they cannot be produced by mixing the others. Primary here means 'not made from anything else', the root sense of primus.
senses.whyCN: 色彩理论把某些色相视为不可再分：它们不能由其他颜色混合产生。这里 primary 意为“不是由别物制成”，是 primus 的根本义。

intro.en: Primary comes straight from Latin primarius, 'of the first rank', built on primus 'first'. English uses it for rank, for sequence, for schooling, and for anything that is not derived from something else.
intro.cn: primary 直接来自拉丁语 primarius“第一等的”，建立在 primus“第一”之上。英语用它表等级、次序、学校教育，以及任何不是由他物派生的事物。

items.en: First recorded in English with the sense 'first in order, original, principal'.
items.cn: 最早在英语中记录为“次序第一、原始的、主要的”。

items.en: From Latin primarius 'of the first rank or quality', from primus 'first'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 primarius“第一等或第一品质的”，源出 primus“第一”。

items.en: primus is traced to PIE *per- 'before, first', also behind prime, prior, and prince. The reconstruction is standard.
items.cn: primus 被追溯到原始印欧语 *per-“在前、第一”，也见于 prime、prior、prince。该重构是通行说法。

items.en: The educational sense 'elementary' and the logical sense 'original, not derived' become established.
items.cn: 教育义“初级的”与逻辑义“原始的、非派生的”确立。

items.en: The noun primary for a direct nominating election appears in American politics.
items.cn: 名词 primary 指直接提名选举，出现在美国政治中。

items.en: Modern English spreads the word across medicine, chemistry, biology, and color theory, always keeping the ordinal core.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词铺到医学、化学、生物学与色彩理论，始终保留序数核心。

note.en: The first group shares the primus stem; the second is about adjectives that also mean chief or first.
note.cn: 第一组共享 primus 词干，第二组看同样表示“首要”或“第一”的形容词。

entries.definition: mainly; chiefly. It is primary plus -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 主要地；首要地。它是 primary 加 -ly。

entries.definition: the state of being first in rank. It comes from Latin primatus.
entries.definitionCN: 首位；优先。来自拉丁语 primatus。

entries.definition: first in rank or quality; also a peak state. It shares primus directly.
entries.definitionCN: 第一等的；鼎盛状态。它直接共享 primus。

entries.definition: first in importance. It is close to primary sense 1 but is not used for stages or schooling.
entries.definitionCN: 重要性第一的。它接近 primary 第 1 义，但不用于阶段或教育。

entries.definition: at the very beginning. It marks sequence only, not rank.
entries.definitionCN: 在最开始的。它只标记次序，不标记等级。

entries.definition: of the simplest level. It matches the schooling sense but not the 'chief' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 最简层次的。它对应教育义，不对应“首要”义。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin primus 'first', the primarius rank word, the primary/principal pair, and the primary source idea.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 primus“第一”、primarius 的等级义、primary 与 principal 这对词，以及“原始资料”概念。

normal.en: Primus means 'first'. Everything primary is first in some line: rank, time, school, or origin.
normal.cn: primus 意为“第一”。一切 primary 都在某条线上第一：等级、时间、学校或起源。

normal.en: Primary vs principal: both mean chief, but only primary is used for stages, schools, and sources.
normal.cn: primary 与 principal：两者都指首要，但只有 primary 用于阶段、学校与资料。

normal.en: Primary source is first-hand evidence; secondary source is commentary on it.
normal.cn: 原始资料是第一手证据；二手资料是对它的评论。

normal.en: Primary school is the first tier of schooling, not a school that is 'more important' than others.
normal.cn: 小学是教育的第一层，不是“比别的学校更重要”的学校。

normal.en: In chemistry, primary, secondary, and tertiary are positions on a carbon chain, numbered from the end.
normal.cn: 化学中，伯、仲、叔是碳链上的位置，从末端编号。

abstract.en: Priority is a spatial metaphor: we place one thing at the front of a line and call it first.
abstract.cn: 优先是一种空间隐喻：我们把一件事放到队伍最前，称它为第一。

abstract.en: The first is not always the best: primary means earliest, and earliest often means simplest.
abstract.cn: 最先的未必最好：primary 意为最早，而最早往往意味着最简单。

abstract.en: A primary source is powerful because it has not yet been interpreted; it is the world before commentary.
abstract.cn: 原始资料之所以有力，是因为它尚未被解释；它是评论之前的世界。

examples.en: Public safety is the primary goal of the policy.
examples.cn: 公共安全是这项政策的首要目标。

examples.en: The study relies on primary sources from the period.
examples.cn: 这项研究依赖该时期的一手资料。

examples.en: He won the primary by a narrow margin.
examples.cn: 他以微弱优势赢得初选。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑来马瑞”——扑过来的马群里，第一匹最显眼 → primary 首要的、第一的

root: 拉丁语 primarius“第一等的”，源出 primus“第一”；更早为原始印欧语 *per-“在前、第一”。同族有 prime、prior、prince。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of primary, all ordinal: first in rank, in time, in school, in evidence, in a chemical chain, or in a color system. The word always places something at the head of a line.
sensesIntro.cn: primary 的九个义项都是序数性的：在等级、时间、学校、证据、化学链或颜色系统中排第一。这个词总是把某物放在一条线的头部。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first position at the head of a line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条线最前端的第一位置。

branches.en: RANK: the most important item is placed first and the rest measured against it.
branches.cn: 等级：最重要的项被放在第一，其余以它为参照。

branches.en: SEQUENCE: the first stage in time, including the first election of a campaign.
branches.cn: 次序：时间上的第一阶段，包括竞选的第一场选举。

branches.en: SCHOOL: the first tier of education, basic rather than advanced.
branches.cn: 学校：教育的第一层，基础而非高级。

branches.en: ORIGIN: first-hand evidence and underived colors are not made from anything else.
branches.cn: 起源：第一手证据与不可再分的原色不是由他物制成。

branches.en: ANATOMY AND CHEMISTRY: the ordinal sense becomes naming for leading feathers and chain positions.
branches.cn: 解剖与化学：序数义变成对前缘飞羽与链上位置的命名。

intro.en: Primary is an adjective and a noun. English adds -ly and -cy, and the primus root also gives prime, primer, and prince.
intro.cn: primary 既是形容词也是名词。英语加 -ly 与 -cy，primus 词根还生成 prime、primer、prince。

latinIntro.en: Latin primarius 'of the first rank' and primus 'first' sit beside primatus 'first place' and principium 'beginning'. The family is about ordinal priority.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 primarius“第一等”与 primus“第一”旁边是 primatus“首位”与 principium“开端”。这个词族关乎序数优先。

the state of being first in rank or importance

definition_zh: 原则；原理；准则；道义；（机器的）工作原理；本源（古义）
definition_en: a basic truth, rule, or belief that explains or guides how something works or how one should act
core_image: 一座建筑的承重柱：看不见整体，却撑着上面所有楼层
scene: 工程师向客户解释这台发动机。Fuel burns, the piston moves, and the crank turns: the same principle drives every model in the catalogue.
sceneCN: 这里 principle 是「原理」（第 3、4 个义项：解释事物如何运作的基本道理；系统工作原理）；句意：燃料燃烧、活塞运动、曲轴转动，同一个原理驱动目录里的每一种型号。图中可辨识物件：发动机剖面、活塞、曲轴、燃烧室、示意图。

pos.zh: 原则；原理；准则；道义；本源（古义）

senses.title: A fundamental truth or rule
senses.definition: a basic rule or truth that other rules depend on
senses.definitionCN: 其他规则所依赖的基本规则或真理
senses.example: The course teaches the principles of economics.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课讲授经济学原理。
senses.why: Latin principium means 'a beginning, a first part'. A principle is where a subject starts: the first thing you must accept before the rest can be built.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 principium 意为“开端、第一部分”。principle 是一门学科的起点：在其余部分建立之前，你必须先接受的那第一件事。

senses.title: A moral rule of conduct
senses.definition: a belief about right behavior that guides a person
senses.definitionCN: 指导人行为的关于正当行为的信念
senses.example: She refused on principle to lie.
senses.exampleCN: 她出于原则拒绝撒谎。
senses.why: Morality turns the architectural image into a personal one: a principle is a load-bearing belief. Break it and the rest of the person's conduct must be rebuilt.
senses.whyCN: 道德把建筑意象变成个人意象：principle 是一根承重的信念。折断它，这个人其余的行为都得重建。

senses.title: A scientific law or mechanism
senses.definition: the basic way a natural process or device works
senses.definitionCN: 自然过程或装置运作的基本方式
senses.example: The principle behind the engine is simple.
senses.exampleCN: 这台发动机背后的原理很简单。
senses.why: Science uses the word for the explanatory core: not a specific result but the rule that generates results. The principle is what remains true across cases.
senses.whyCN: 科学用这个词指解释的核心：不是某个具体结果，而是产生结果的规则。原理是在各种情形中都成立的东西。

senses.title: The working rule of a system
senses.definition: the rule by which a machine, method, or organization operates
senses.definitionCN: 机器、方法或组织运作所依的规则
senses.example: The pump works on the principle of expanding air.
senses.exampleCN: 这个泵依空气膨胀的原理工作。
senses.why: Engineering names the operating rule of an artifact. The principle explains why the design works, which is why it can be transferred to new machines.
senses.whyCN: 工程学给人工物的运作规则命名。原理解释设计为何有效，因此可以迁移到新机器上。

senses.title: A personal code of conduct
senses.definition: a set of values a person has decided to live by
senses.definitionCN: 一个人决定遵行的价值体系
senses.example: He is a man of principle.
senses.exampleCN: 他是一个有原则的人。
senses.why: When a person owns principles, the word becomes a character description. To have principles is to have a structure that does not bend with convenience.
senses.whyCN: 当一个人拥有 principles，这个词就成了一种品格描述。有原则，就是有一套不随便利弯曲的结构。

senses.title: Origin or source (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, the beginning or source from which something comes
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：事物由来的开端或源头
senses.example: Water was once held to be the principle of all things.
senses.exampleCN: 水曾被当作万物的本源。
senses.why: The oldest sense is 'beginning'. Greek philosophy asked for the arche, the first principle of things, and English used principle for that source before it narrowed to rules.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是“开端”。希腊哲学追问万物的 arche（第一原理），英语在收窄为“规则”之前，曾用 principle 指那个源头。

senses.title: In principle: as a theory
senses.definition: in the phrase in principle, as far as the basic idea is concerned
senses.definitionCN: 用于 in principle，就基本理念而言
senses.example: In principle the plan is sound.
senses.exampleCN: 原则上这个计划是合理的。
senses.why: The phrase separates theory from practice: the principle may hold even if the execution fails. It is a way of granting the idea without promising the result.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把理论与实行分开：即使执行失败，原理仍可成立。它是一种承认想法、却不承诺结果的说法。

senses.title: On principle: from conviction
senses.definition: in the phrase on principle, because of a moral or personal rule
senses.definitionCN: 用于 on principle，出于道德或个人规则
senses.example: He opposed the deal on principle.
senses.exampleCN: 他出于原则反对这笔交易。
senses.why: On principle marks a decision that is not pragmatic. The person is not weighing outcomes but obeying a rule, which is exactly what a principle is for.
senses.whyCN: on principle 标记一个非务实的选择。人不是在权衡结果，而是在服从规则——这正是原则的用途。

senses.title: A constituent element (archaic science)
senses.definition: in old chemistry and philosophy, a basic substance from which things are made
senses.definitionCN: 旧化学与哲学中构成事物的基本物质
senses.example: The four principles of the old chemistry were earth, water, air, and fire.
senses.exampleCN: 旧化学的四种要素是土、水、气、火。
senses.why: Before modern chemistry, 'principles' were the simple bodies into which matter could be resolved. The word then meant both beginning and ingredient.
senses.whyCN: 在现代化学之前，principles 是物质可被分解成的基本体。那时这个词兼指“开端”与“成分”。

intro.en: Principle comes from Latin principium, 'a beginning'. Its root princeps means 'first man', from primus 'first' plus capere 'to take'. The same root gives prince and principal, which is why principle and principal are so often confused.
intro.cn: principle 来自拉丁语 principium“开端”。其词根 princeps 意为“第一人”，由 primus“第一”加 capere“取”构成。同一个词根生成 prince 与 principal，所以 principle 与 principal 常被混淆。

items.en: First recorded as 'origin, source, fundamental truth', from Latin principium through Old French principe.
items.cn: 最早记录为“起源、源头、根本真理”，经古法语 principe 来自拉丁语 principium。

items.en: principium 'beginning, first part' comes from princeps 'first, chief', literally 'one who takes first place'.
items.cn: principium“开端、第一部分”来自 princeps“第一的、首要的”，字面为“占据第一位者”。

items.en: princeps = primus 'first' + capere 'to take, seize'. The chief is the one who takes the first place or the first share.
items.cn: princeps = primus“第一”+ capere“取、抓”。首领就是占据第一位或第一份的人。

items.en: principle comes from principium (a beginning, a rule); principal comes from principalis (first in rank). They share princeps but differ in meaning: a principle is a rule, a principal is a chief or a sum of money.
items.cn: principle 来自 principium（开端、规则）；principal 来自 principalis（等级第一）。它们共享 princeps，但含义不同：principle 是规则，principal 是首领或本金。

items.en: The moral sense 'a rule of right conduct' becomes common.
items.cn: 道德义“正当行为的规则”变得常见。

items.en: Modern English keeps principle for rules and truths, and principal for heads, main things, and sums of money.
items.cn: 现代英语用 principle 指规则与真理，用 principal 指校长、主要事物与本金。

note.en: The first group shares the princeps stem and the dangerous principle/principal pair; the second is about words that also mean a rule or truth.
note.cn: 第一组共享 princeps 词干与易混的 principle/principal 对，第二组看同样表示“规则”或“真理”的词。

entries.definition: chief; a school head; a sum of money. It comes from principalis, not principium.
entries.definitionCN: 主要的；校长；本金。它来自 principalis，而非 principium。

entries.definition: acting according to moral principles. It is principle plus -ed.
entries.definitionCN: 按道德原则行事的。它是 principle 加 -ed。

entries.definition: a royal ruler, from princeps 'first man'.
entries.definitionCN: 王子；亲王，来自 princeps“第一人”。

entries.definition: a statement about what must be done or what happens. It is broader and less foundational than principle.
entries.definitionCN: 关于必须做什么或会发生什么的陈述。它比 principle 更宽、更少基础性。

entries.definition: a binding rule, or a regular natural pattern. It is enforced or observed, not merely believed.
entries.definitionCN: 有约束力的规则，或自然规律。它被强制执行或被观察，而不只是被相信。

entries.definition: a set of beliefs taught by an authority. It is collective and official, unlike a personal principle.
entries.definitionCN: 权威所教的一套信念。它是集体、官方的，不同于个人原则。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin principium 'beginning', princeps = primus + capere, the principle/principal pair, and the phrases in principle and on principle.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 principium“开端”、princeps = primus + capere、principle 与 principal 这对词，以及 in principle / on principle 两个短语。

normal.en: Principium means 'beginning'. A principle is where a subject begins: the first thing you must accept.
normal.cn: principium 意为“开端”。principle 是一门学科的起点：你必须先接受的第一件事。

normal.en: Princeps is primus 'first' plus capere 'take': the chief is the one who takes first place.
normal.cn: princeps 是 primus“第一”加 capere“取”：首领就是占据第一位的人。

normal.en: Principle vs principal: a principle is a rule (from principium); a principal is a chief or a sum (from principalis).
normal.cn: principle 与 principal：principle 是规则（来自 principium）；principal 是首领或本金（来自 principalis）。

normal.en: In principle means 'in theory'; on principle means 'from conviction'. One is about ideas, the other about character.
normal.cn: in principle 意为“理论上”；on principle 意为“出于信念”。一个谈想法，一个谈品格。

normal.en: A person of principle is load-bearing: the beliefs hold up the rest of the conduct.
normal.cn: a person of principle 是承重的：这些信念撑起其余的行为。

abstract.en: A principle is a rule you keep when it costs you something; otherwise it is only a preference.
abstract.cn: 原则是付出代价时仍遵守的规则；否则它只是偏好。

abstract.en: Beginnings and rules are the same word because rules are where thought starts, not where it ends.
abstract.cn: 开端与规则是同一个词，因为规则是思想的起点，而非终点。

abstract.en: The principle/principal confusion is instructive: English once used one word for both a beginning and a chief, then split the labor.
abstract.cn: principle/principal 的混淆很有启发：英语曾用一个词兼指开端与首领，后来才分工。

examples.en: The machine works on a simple principle.
examples.cn: 这台机器依一个简单原理工作。

examples.en: She refused to sign on principle.
examples.cn: 她出于原则拒绝签署。

examples.en: In principle, the two systems should be compatible.
examples.cn: 理论上，这两个系统应当兼容。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑润色剖”——先把原则扑在纸上，再润色剖析 → principle 原则、原理

root: 拉丁语 principium“开端”，源出 princeps“第一人”= primus“第一”+ capere“取”。同根异义词：principal（主要的；校长；本金）。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of principle, all versions of 'the first thing'. It can be the first truth of a subject, the first rule of a person, the first mechanism of a machine, or the first source of things.
sensesIntro.cn: principle 的九个义项都是“第一之物”的变体。它可以是学科的第一真理、个人的第一规则、机器的第一机制，或万物的第一源头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a load-bearing first rule that holds up everything built on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根承重的第一规则，撑起其上的一切。

branches.en: FOUNDATION: the basic truth explains how a subject or a natural process works.
branches.cn: 基础：基本真理解释一门学科或一个自然过程如何运作。

branches.en: CONDUCT: a moral rule becomes a personal code and a reason to act.
branches.cn: 行为：道德规则变成个人准则与行动理由。

branches.en: ORIGIN: the archaic sense names the source or constituent of things.
branches.cn: 本源：古义指事物的源头或构成要素。

branches.en: THEORY: in principle separates the idea from its execution.
branches.cn: 理论：in principle 把理念与执行分开。

branches.en: TRANSFER: an operating principle can be moved from one machine to another.
branches.cn: 迁移：工作原理可以从一台机器移到另一台。

intro.en: Principle is a noun from Latin principium. English adds -ed and the negative un-, and the princeps root also gives prince, principal, and principality.
intro.cn: principle 是来自拉丁 principium 的名词。英语加 -ed 与否定 un-，princeps 词根还生成 prince、principal、principality。

latinIntro.en: Latin principium 'beginning' and princeps 'first man' share primus 'first'. Principalis gives principal, while principium gives principle: same family, different jobs.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 principium“开端”与 princeps“第一人”共享 primus“第一”。principalis 生成 principal，principium 生成 principle：同族不同职。

definition_en: earlier in time or order, or higher in importance; also a monastic superior or a previous conviction
core_image: 排队时站在你前面的人，既更早到，也先被叫到

pos.zh: 先前的；更早的；优先的；更重要的
