最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Earlier in time
senses.definition: existing or happening before something else
senses.definitionCN: 比另一事物更早存在或发生
senses.example: She had prior experience in publishing.
senses.exampleCN: 她先前有出版经验。
senses.why: Latin prior is a comparative meaning 'former, first of two'. It compares two points on a line and names the one already passed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 prior 是比较级，意为“前者、两者中的第一个”。它比较线上的两点，命名已经过去的那一点。

senses.title: Preceding in order
senses.definition: coming before in a series or procedure
senses.definitionCN: 在系列或程序中出现得更早
senses.example: No changes may be made without prior approval.
senses.exampleCN: 未经事先批准不得改动。
senses.why: Procedures require gates: the prior step must be completed before the next begins. The word turns sequence into a condition.
senses.whyCN: 程序需要关口：前一步必须完成，下一步才能开始。这个词把次序变成条件。

senses.title: Higher in importance or rank
senses.definition: having a stronger claim or higher rank
senses.definitionCN: 拥有更强的请求权或更高的等级
senses.example: They have a prior claim on the land.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对这块土地有更优先的请求权。
senses.why: The Latin comparative could mean 'superior' as well as 'earlier'. Priority and precedence share the image of standing in front of the line.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁比较级既可指“更早”，也可指“更优越”。优先与居先共享“站在队伍前面”的意象。

senses.title: Before, in the phrase prior to
senses.definition: in formal usage, before a time or event
senses.definitionCN: 正式用法：在某个时间或事件之前
senses.example: Prior to 2010, the firm had no overseas office.
senses.exampleCN: 2010 年之前，这家公司没有海外办事处。
senses.why: Prior to is the formal cousin of before. Legal and academic writing prefer it because it sounds procedural rather than conversational.
senses.whyCN: prior to 是 before 的正式表亲。法律与学术写作偏爱它，因为它听起来像程序而非口语。

senses.title: Presumed or existing earlier
senses.definition: in formal contexts, already held or existing before the present matter
senses.definitionCN: 正式语境中，在当前事项之前已持有或已存在
senses.example: The prior agreement still governs the dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 先前的协议仍管辖这场争议。
senses.why: Law speaks of prior agreements, prior art, and prior rights: things that existed first and therefore constrain what can be done now.
senses.whyCN: 法律谈 prior agreements、prior art、prior rights：先已存在的事物，因此约束当下能做什么。

senses.title: A monastic superior
senses.definition: the head of a priory or a religious house
senses.definitionCN: 小修道院或宗教院舍的首脑
senses.example: The prior welcomed the visitors at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 院长在门口迎接访客。
senses.why: The noun came into English in the 14c. from Medieval Latin prior, 'superior'. The monastic prior stands first in his house, the same rank image as the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词 14 世纪从中世纪拉丁语 prior“上级”进入英语。修道院院长在其院舍中居首，与形容词的等级意象相同。

senses.title: A previous conviction (informal)
senses.definition: in informal legal usage, an earlier criminal conviction
senses.definitionCN: 非正式法律用语：先前的刑事定罪
senses.example: The defendant has two priors.
senses.exampleCN: 被告有两项前科。
senses.why: Police and court slang clip the phrase 'prior conviction' to priors. The word's temporal sense becomes a record that follows a person.
senses.whyCN: 警察与法庭俚语把 prior conviction 缩略为 priors。这个词的时间义变成一份跟随此人的记录。

senses.title: The antecedent in logic
senses.definition: in logic, the proposition from which another is inferred
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑中推出另一命题所依据的前一命题
senses.example: If the prior is false, the conclusion fails.
senses.exampleCN: 如果前件为假，结论就不成立。
senses.why: Inference runs along a line: the prior proposition comes first and licenses the next. The temporal order becomes a relation of support.
senses.whyCN: 推理沿一条线运行：前件在先，并授权后件。时间次序变成支撑关系。

senses.title: Superior in rank (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, of higher rank or dignity
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：等级或尊严更高的
senses.example: the prior rank of a duke
senses.exampleCN: 公爵更高的等级
senses.why: This is the Latin comparative at full strength: prior as 'superior'. Modern English keeps the trace in the noun prior and in the idea of a prior claim.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁比较级的完整力量：prior 即“更优越”。现代英语在名词 prior 与“更优先的请求权”中留下痕迹。

intro.en: Prior entered English twice: first as a noun for a monastic superior, then as an adjective for 'earlier'. Both come from Latin prior, a comparative meaning 'former, first of two', which also gives priority and primacy.
intro.cn: prior 两次进入英语：先作名词指修道院院长，后作形容词指“更早”。两者都来自拉丁语 prior——一个意为“前者、两者中第一”的比较级，它也生成 priority 与 primacy。

items.en: The noun is first recorded for the superior of a priory or religious house, from Medieval Latin prior.
items.cn: 名词最早记录指小修道院或宗教院舍的上级，来自中世纪拉丁语 prior。

items.en: Latin prior 'former, previous, first of two' is a comparative of an old adjective *pri- 'before'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 prior“前者、先前的、两者中第一”是古形容词 *pri-“在前”的比较级。

items.en: The root is traced to PIE *per- 'before, first', also behind first, prime, and principal. The reconstruction is standard.
items.cn: 词根被追溯到原始印欧语 *per-“在前、第一”，也见于 first、prime、principal。该重构是通行说法。

items.en: The adjective is recorded in English with the sense 'earlier, previous'.
items.cn: 形容词在英语中记录为“更早的、先前的”。

items.en: prior to becomes a formal preposition, and the legal phrase prior claim spreads.
items.cn: prior to 成为正式介词，法律短语 prior claim 传播开来。

items.en: Modern English keeps the religious noun and the temporal adjective side by side, plus the informal plural priors for convictions.
items.cn: 现代英语让宗教名词与时间形容词并存，另有口语复数 priors 指前科。

note.en: The first group shares the prior/priority stem; the second is about words that also mean earlier or more important.
note.cn: 第一组共享 prior/priority 词干，第二组看同样表示“更早”或“更重要”的词。

entries.definition: the state of being first in rank or the thing ranked first. It comes from Medieval Latin prioritas.
entries.definitionCN: 优先地位；优先事项。来自中世纪拉丁语 prioritas。

entries.definition: a small monastery headed by a prior.
entries.definitionCN: 由院长主持的小修道院。

entries.definition: a female superior of a priory.
entries.definitionCN: 女修道院院长。

entries.definition: earlier, especially the one just before. It is less formal than prior.
entries.definitionCN: 更早的，尤指刚过去的那一个。它比 prior 少些正式。

entries.definition: the earlier of two, or a past role-holder. It contrasts with latter.
entries.definitionCN: 两者中在前的，或前任。与 latter 相对。

entries.definition: coming immediately before in order. It is purely positional.
entries.definitionCN: 在次序上紧接其前。它纯粹是位置性的。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin prior as a comparative, the noun for a monastic superior, the phrase prior to, and the legal sense of a prior claim.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 prior 的比较级性质、指修道院院长的名词、短语 prior to，以及 prior claim 的法律义。

normal.en: Prior is a Latin comparative: it compares two things and names the earlier one.
normal.cn: prior 是拉丁比较级：它比较两物，并命名更早的那一个。

normal.en: The same comparative can mean 'superior', which is why prior also means 'more important'.
normal.cn: 同一比较级也可指“更优越”，所以 prior 也表“更重要”。

normal.en: The noun prior is a different borrowing: the head of a priory stands first in his house.
normal.cn: 名词 prior 是另一次借入：小修道院院长在其院舍中居首。

normal.en: Prior to is formal 'before'; lawyers and academics prefer it to sound procedural.
normal.cn: prior to 是正式的 before；律师与学者偏爱它，以显得程序化。

normal.en: In police slang, priors are prior convictions: the past that follows a person.
normal.cn: 警察俚语中，priors 是前科：跟随一个人的过去。

abstract.en: Time and rank collapse into one word: what came first is assumed to deserve first place.
abstract.cn: 时间与等级在此塌缩成一个词：先来的，被假定该先得。

abstract.en: A prior claim is a promise the past makes to the present.
abstract.cn: 优先请求权是过去对当下作出的承诺。

abstract.en: The comparative form is the point: prior never stands alone, it always implies a second term.
abstract.cn: 重点在比较级形式：prior 从不孤立，它总隐含另一个项。

examples.en: You need prior approval before changing the budget.
examples.cn: 改动预算前需要事先批准。

examples.en: Prior to joining the firm, she taught at a university.
examples.cn: 加入这家公司之前，她在大学任教。

examples.en: The court considered his prior convictions.
examples.cn: 法庭考虑了他的前科。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑来尔”——先扑过来排队的那一个 → prior 先前的、优先的

root: 拉丁语 prior“前者、两者中第一”，是 *pri-“在前”的比较级；更早为原始印欧语 *per-。同族有 priority、prime、principal。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of prior, all comparative. The word always implies a second term: this one is earlier, or higher, or both. It can point to a time, a rank, a right, a monastic office, or a criminal record.
sensesIntro.cn: prior 的九个义项都是比较性的。这个词总隐含另一个项：这一个更早，或更高，或两者兼有。它可以指时间、等级、权利、修道职务或犯罪记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the one standing earlier in the line, and therefore first in line.
core.cn: 核心意象：在队伍中站得更早、因而更靠前的那一个。

branches.en: TIME: an earlier point or step, including agreements already in force.
branches.cn: 时间：更早的时间点或步骤，包括已生效的协议。

branches.en: RANK: the comparative shades into superiority and precedence.
branches.cn: 等级：比较级滑向优越与居先。

branches.en: PREPOSITION: prior to is the formal 'before'.
branches.cn: 介词：prior to 是正式的“在……之前”。

branches.en: OFFICE: the monastic prior stands first in his house.
branches.cn: 职务：修道院院长在其院舍中居首。

branches.en: RECORD AND LOGIC: prior convictions, and the antecedent proposition.
branches.cn: 记录与逻辑：前科，以及逻辑前件。

intro.en: Prior is both adjective and noun. English adds -ity, -ize, and -y, and the Latin comparative also underlies priority and primacy.
intro.cn: prior 既是形容词也是名词。英语加 -ity、-ize、-y，拉丁比较级还支撑 priority 与 primacy。

latinIntro.en: Latin prior 'former, first of two' is a comparative beside primus 'first' and *pri- 'before'. Its noun prioritas gives English priority.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 prior“前者、两者中第一”是与 primus“第一”、*pri-“在前”相邻的比较级。其名词 prioritas 生成英语 priority。

items.meaning: first place in rank; a thing ranked first
items.meaningCN: 优先；优先事项（-ity 构成名词）

items.meaning: to treat as more important than others
items.meaningCN: 优先处理（-ize 构成动词）

items.meaning: the act of ranking things by importance
a monastery headed by a prior
a female monastic superior
the office or term of a prior
previous convictions, informal
relating to a prior
first in rank or time

latinEntries.meaningCN: 前者；先前的；两者中第一

definition_zh: 优先；优先权；优先事项；优先次序；（计算机）优先级
definition_en: the state of being more important than something else, or a thing that is ranked first
core_image: 急诊分诊台上，红色标签的伤员先被推进手术室
scene: 医院分诊时，护士把红黄绿标签贴在病历夹上。The triage nurse set the priority of each patient by colour, so the most serious cases were seen first.
sceneCN: 这里 priority 是「优先次序、优先级」（第 3 个义项：按重要性排出的先后顺序）；句意：分诊护士用颜色给每位病人排定优先次序，最危重的先看。图中可辨识物件：分诊台、红黄绿标签、担架、病历夹、时钟。

pos.zh: 优先；优先权；优先事项；优先次序

derivatives.zh: 优先处理；按优先级排序

senses.title: The thing ranked first
senses.definition: the thing that is treated as most important
senses.definitionCN: 被当作最重要的事情
senses.example: Patient safety is our top priority.
senses.exampleCN: 病人安全是我们的头等大事。
senses.why: Priority is the noun of prior: it names whatever stands first in a line. In modern management, that first thing is often called a priority in the plural.
senses.whyCN: priority 是 prior 的名词：它命名排在队伍最前的东西。现代管理中，这个“第一之物”常用复数 priorities 表示。

senses.title: The state of being more important
senses.definition: the condition of having a stronger claim than others
senses.definitionCN: 拥有比其余更强的地位
senses.example: The issue has priority over all others.
senses.exampleCN: 这个议题优先于其余一切。
senses.why: The word can name a status rather than a thing: something has priority. It is a relation, not an object, and it always implies competitors.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以命名状态而非事物：某物具有 priority。它是一种关系，不是物件，而且总隐含竞争者。

senses.title: An order of precedence
senses.definition: a ranking that decides what is handled first
senses.definitionCN: 决定先处理什么的排序
senses.example: The committee set its priorities for the year.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会定下了年度优先次序。
senses.why: Once several items compete, priority becomes a list. The plural is natural here: a set of ranked claims, not one favourite.
senses.whyCN: 一旦多项事务竞争，priority 就变成一份列表。复数在此很自然：一组被排序的诉求，而非一个宠儿。

senses.title: The right to go first
senses.definition: the right of a vehicle or person to move before others
senses.definitionCN: 车辆或人先于他人行动的权利
senses.example: Bicycles have priority at this crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 自行车在这个路口有优先通行权。
senses.why: Traffic rules codify the line: priority marks who may move first. The metaphor becomes legal and physical at the same time.
senses.whyCN: 交通规则把队伍编码：priority 标记谁可以先动。这个隐喻同时变成法律与物理的。

senses.title: Ceremonial precedence
senses.definition: the rank order of people at a formal occasion
senses.definitionCN: 正式场合中人们的位次顺序
senses.example: The ambassador's priority in the procession was fixed.
senses.exampleCN: 大使在行列中的位次是固定的。
senses.why: Court and diplomacy rank bodies in space: who enters first, who sits nearest. Priority is the abstract name for that spatial order.
senses.whyCN: 宫廷与外交按空间给人排序：谁先进、谁坐得最近。priority 是那种空间秩序的抽象名称。

senses.title: A computing priority level
senses.definition: a value that decides how soon a task is serviced
senses.definitionCN: 决定任务多快被处理的一个值
senses.example: The process runs at high priority.
senses.exampleCN: 这个进程以高优先级运行。
senses.why: Operating systems borrow the queue image: every task waits, and priority decides who jumps ahead. It is the same ranking, made numeric.
senses.whyCN: 操作系统借用排队意象：每个任务都在等，优先级决定谁插到前面。还是同一个排序，只是变成数字。

senses.title: Top priority
senses.definition: the single most urgent item, in the phrase top priority
senses.definitionCN: 短语 top priority：唯一最紧迫的事项
senses.example: Rebuilding the bridge is a top priority.
senses.exampleCN: 重建桥梁是首要任务。
senses.why: Top priority doubles the ranking: top already means first, priority already means first. The redundancy marks urgency, which is why it is so common in politics.
senses.whyCN: top priority 重复了排序：top 已是第一，priority 已是第一。这种冗余标记紧迫性，所以它在政治语言中如此常见。

senses.title: Low priority
senses.definition: an item that can wait, in the phrase low priority
senses.definitionCN: 短语 low priority：可以等待的事项
senses.example: The paint job is a low priority this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年粉刷是次要事项。
senses.why: The scale runs from top to low. Low priority is not unimportant but postponable: the item stays in the queue, just further back.
senses.whyCN: 这个尺度从 top 到 low。low priority 不是不重要，而是可推迟：事项仍在队列里，只是更靠后。

senses.title: Earlier status in time (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, the state of being earlier in time
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：在时间上更早的状态
senses.example: The priority of the claim depended on its date.
senses.exampleCN: 这项权利的在先性取决于它的日期。
senses.why: The oldest sense was temporal: priority meant being earlier. Modern English keeps the temporal trace mainly in law, where an earlier filing wins.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是时间性的：priority 指更早。现代英语主要在法律中保留时间痕迹：先提交者胜。

intro.en: Priority is the noun of prior, formed in Medieval Latin as prioritas. It began as 'the state of being earlier' and grew into 'the right to be first', which is why both time and rank live inside it.
intro.cn: priority 是 prior 的名词，在中世纪拉丁语中作 prioritas。它始于“更早的状态”，发展为“居先的权利”，所以时间与等级都住在它里面。

items.en: First recorded in English with the sense 'the state of being earlier or prior'.
items.cn: 最早在英语中记录为“更早或在先的状态”。

items.en: From prioritas 'priority, precedence', from Latin prior 'former, first of two'.
items.cn: 来自中世纪拉丁语 prioritas“优先、居先”，源出拉丁语 prior“前者、两者中第一”。

items.en: prior is a comparative of *pri- 'before', from PIE *per- 'before, first'.
items.cn: prior 是 *pri-“在前”的比较级，更早为原始印欧语 *per-“在前、第一”。

items.en: The sense widens from temporal precedence to rank and ceremonial order.
items.cn: 义项从时间上的在先扩展到等级与礼仪次序。

items.en: Management and administration make priority a countable item: priorities are things to be ranked.
items.cn: 管理与行政把 priority 变成可数事项：priorities 是待排序的东西。

items.en: Modern English also uses priority in computing, traffic law, and diplomacy, wherever a queue needs a rule.
items.cn: 现代英语还把 priority 用于计算机、交通法与外交，凡队列需要规则之处皆可。

note.en: The first group shares the prior stem; the second is about words that also mean precedence or importance.
note.cn: 第一组共享 prior 词干，第二组看同样表示“居先”或“重要”的词。

entries.definition: earlier or more important. It is the adjective behind priority.
entries.definitionCN: 更早或更重要的。它是 priority 背后的形容词。

entries.definition: to rank things and act on the first one.
entries.definitionCN: 排序并先处理第一项。

entries.definition: the act of ranking by importance.
entries.definitionCN: 按重要性排序的行为。

entries.definition: the right to go before others, especially in ceremony. It stresses order, not urgency.
entries.definitionCN: 先于他人的权利，尤用于礼仪。它强调次序，而非紧迫。

entries.definition: a liking for one thing over another. It is personal taste, not a ranked obligation.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物胜过另一物的喜爱。它是个人偏好，不是排序义务。

entries.definition: the quality of needing immediate action. It explains why something is a priority.
entries.definitionCN: 需要立即行动的性质。它解释某事为何成为优先。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Medieval Latin prioritas, the prior/priority pair, triage and traffic uses, and the phrases top priority and low priority.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：中世纪拉丁语 prioritas、prior 与 priority 这对词、分诊与交通用法，以及 top priority / low priority 两个短语。

normal.en: Priority is prior plus -ity: it names whatever stands first in the line.
normal.cn: priority 是 prior 加 -ity：它命名排在队伍最前的东西。

normal.en: It can be a thing (a priority) or a status (to have priority). The first is countable, the second is relational.
normal.cn: 它可以是事物（a priority），也可以是状态（to have priority）。前者可数，后者是关系。

normal.en: Triage is priority in action: red tags move first, green tags wait.
normal.cn: 分诊是 priority 的实战：红标先走，绿标等待。

normal.en: Top priority is deliberately redundant; the doubling signals urgency in political speech.
normal.cn: top priority 是刻意冗余；这种重复在政治语言中标记紧迫。

normal.en: Low priority does not mean unimportant: it means postponable, still in the queue.
normal.cn: low priority 不是不重要：它意味着可推迟，仍在队列里。

abstract.en: Priority is scarcity made visible: when time or space is limited, someone must be ranked above someone else.
abstract.cn: 优先是稀缺的可见化：当时间或空间有限，总得有人被排在别人之上。

abstract.en: Every ranking is an argument about values disguised as a schedule.
abstract.cn: 每一种排序都是伪装成日程的价值争论。

abstract.en: The word began as 'earlier' and became 'more important'; modern life quietly assumes the first deserves the second.
abstract.cn: 这个词从“更早”变成“更重要”；现代生活悄悄假定先来的理应优先。

examples.en: The safety of children must take priority over cost.
examples.cn: 儿童安全必须优先于成本。

examples.en: Deciding priorities is the hardest part of the job.
examples.cn: 决定优先次序是这份工作最难的部分。

examples.en: Emergency vehicles have priority at the junction.
examples.cn: 紧急车辆在交叉口有优先通行权。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑来奥瑞提”——先扑过来的那一个，奥瑞提先被叫号 → priority 优先、优先事项

root: 中世纪拉丁语 prioritas“优先、居先”，源出拉丁语 prior“前者、两者中第一”，再上为 *pri- / PIE *per-“在前”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of priority, all about a queue. The queue can be moral (top priority), legal (the right of way), ceremonial (order of procession), or digital (a process level).
sensesIntro.cn: priority 的九个义项都关于一条队列。这条队列可以是道德的（头等大事）、法律的（通行权）、礼仪的（行列位次）或数字的（进程等级）。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ranked queue in which one item is served first.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条被排序的队列，其中一项先被服务。

branches.en: FIRST CLAIM: one thing is treated as more important, whether named or as a status.
branches.cn: 第一诉求：某物被当作更重要，无论作为事项还是状态。

branches.en: ORDER: several claims are ranked into a list or a ceremonial sequence.
branches.cn: 次序：多项诉求被排成列表或礼仪序列。

branches.en: TRAFFIC: the ranking becomes a right to move first.
branches.cn: 交通：排序变成先行动的权利。

branches.en: COMPUTING: the queue is numeric, and priority decides which task jumps ahead.
branches.cn: 计算机：队列变成数字，优先级决定哪个任务插队。

branches.en: SCALE AND TIME: top and low mark urgency, while the archaic sense keeps the temporal origin.
branches.cn: 尺度与时间：top 与 low 标记紧迫，古义保留时间起源。

intro.en: Priority is a noun from Medieval Latin prioritas. English adds -ize, -ation, and -ed, and the base prior also gives priory and prioress.
intro.cn: priority 是来自中世纪拉丁 prioritas 的名词。英语加 -ize、-ation、-ed，词基 prior 还生成 priory 与 prioress。

latinIntro.en: Latin prior 'former' and prioritas 'precedence' sit beside primus 'first'. The family ranks things along a line from earlier to more important.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 prior“前者”与 prioritas“居先”旁边是 primus“第一”。这个词族沿一条从“更早”到“更重要”的线给事物排序。

definition_zh: 继续进行；前进；着手；推进；（法律）起诉；发出（古义）
definition_en: to continue or move forward, especially after a pause or as the next step
core_image: 一条路在岔口干等，绿灯亮起后脚步重新向前
scene: 演示暂停后，主持人拿起翻页笔。The host said we may proceed to the next slide, and the screen changed as soon as the button was pressed.
sceneCN: 这里 proceed 是「继续进行、进入下一步」（第 1 个义项：停顿之后接着往下走）；句意：主持人说我们可以继续看下一张幻灯片，按钮一按屏幕就换了画面。图中可辨识物件：投影屏、翻页笔、讲台、水杯、听众。

pos.zh: 继续进行；前进；着手；推进；（法律）起诉

senses.title: Continue after a pause
senses.definition: to continue doing something after stopping or waiting
senses.definitionCN: 停止或等待之后继续做某事
senses.example: After a short break, we proceeded with the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 短暂休息后，我们继续开会。
senses.why: Latin procedere means 'go forward': pro- 'forward' plus cedere 'go'. The word assumes something has stopped and now resumes its motion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 procedere 意为“向前走”：pro-“向前”加 cedere“走”。这个词假定某物曾停下，现在重新开始运动。

senses.title: Move forward physically
senses.definition: to move onward in space
senses.definitionCN: 在空间中向前移动
senses.example: The procession proceeded slowly down the street.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍沿街缓慢行进。
senses.why: This is the literal core: feet or wheels moving along a path. Everything abstract in English is borrowed from this simple forward motion.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面的核心：脚或轮子沿路移动。英语里一切抽象义都从这个简单的向前运动借来。

senses.title: Begin or undertake an action
senses.definition: to start doing something as the next step
senses.definitionCN: 作为下一步开始做某事
senses.example: We will proceed to build the prototype.
senses.exampleCN: 我们将着手制作原型。
senses.why: Starting and continuing are close: the next step is both the end of waiting and the beginning of action. The infinitive after proceed marks what is undertaken.
senses.whyCN: 开始与继续很近：下一步既是等待的结束，也是行动的开始。proceed 后接不定式，标记着手的内容。

senses.title: Carry out a plan or process
senses.definition: to carry on with a plan, process, or procedure
senses.definitionCN: 继续推进计划、过程或程序
senses.example: The committee proceeded according to the rules.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会按规则推进。
senses.why: Institutions need a script: proceed means to follow the prescribed steps. The word becomes procedural, which is why procedure is its close relative.
senses.whyCN: 机构需要脚本：proceed 意为按既定步骤走。这个词变得程序化，所以 procedure 是它的近亲。

senses.title: Make progress
senses.definition: to advance toward a goal
senses.definitionCN: 朝目标推进
senses.example: The project is proceeding well.
senses.exampleCN: 项目进展顺利。
senses.why: Forward motion becomes achievement: if the path advances, the work advances. English uses the same metaphor for time, work, and journeys.
senses.whyCN: 向前运动变成成就：路推进，工作就推进。英语用同一个隐喻说时间、工作与旅程。

senses.title: Go on to the next item
senses.definition: in formal speech, to move to the next topic or stage
senses.definitionCN: 正式讲话中，进入下一个话题或阶段
senses.example: Let us proceed to the second question.
senses.exampleCN: 让我们进入第二个问题。
senses.why: Meetings rank items in order. Proceed is the verbal signal that one item is closed and the next opened, a procedural gate rather than a physical one.
senses.whyCN: 会议把议题排序。proceed 是“上一项已关、下一项已开”的口头信号，是程序的关口而非物理关口。

senses.title: Take legal action against
senses.definition: to start or continue a legal action against someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某人开始或继续法律诉讼
senses.example: The company proceeded against the supplier.
senses.exampleCN: 公司对供应商提起诉讼。
senses.why: Law is a path with formal steps: filing, hearing, judgment. To proceed against someone is to set that machinery in motion.
senses.whyCN: 法律是一条有正式步骤的路：提交、听证、判决。proceed against 某人，就是启动这套机器。

senses.title: Come forth or issue from (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, to originate or come out from a source
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：从某个源头产生或出来
senses.example: Light proceeds from the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 光来自太阳。
senses.why: The Latin verb could mean 'come out of'. English kept this for a time: what proceeds from a source moves out of it. Modern usage prefers arise or issue.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词可指“从……出来”。英语保留过一阵：proceed from 某源，就是从它里面出来。现代多用 arise 或 issue。

senses.title: (Of an event) go forward
senses.definition: of an event or plan, to take place as arranged
senses.definitionCN: 事件或计划按安排进行
senses.example: The wedding will proceed despite the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管下雨，婚礼仍将举行。
senses.why: An event is treated as an object on a path: it can be stopped, delayed, or allowed to proceed. The word grants permission to the future.
senses.whyCN: 事件被当作路上的物件：它可以被停下、推迟，或被允许 proceed。这个词是在给未来发放许可。

intro.en: Proceed is a pure motion word: pro- 'forward' plus cedere 'go'. English borrowed it in the late 14c. and then extended the walk into meetings, projects, and lawsuits.
intro.cn: proceed 是一个纯粹的运动词：pro-“向前”加 cedere“走”。英语在 14 世纪末借入，随后把这场行走扩展到会议、项目与诉讼。

items.en: First recorded with the sense 'go forward, continue one's course'.
items.cn: 最早记录为“向前走、继续行程”。

items.en: From Latin procedere 'go forward, advance, come forth' = pro- 'forward' + cedere 'go, yield'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 procedere“向前走、推进、出现”= pro-“向前”+ cedere“走、让”。

items.en: cedere also gives cede, accede, concede, exceed, precede, and succeed. The base is about going or yielding, and the prefix pro- points the going forward.
items.cn: cedere 还生成 cede、accede、concede、exceed、precede、succeed。词基关乎走或让，前缀 pro- 把方向指向前。

items.en: The legal sense 'begin or carry on an action at law' develops, producing proceedings and procedure.
items.cn: 法律义“开始或继续诉讼”发展出来，产生 proceedings 与 procedure。

items.en: Modern English uses proceed for meetings, projects, and formal sequences, always with a sense of a path resumed.
items.cn: 现代英语用 proceed 指会议、项目与正式流程，始终带有“路径重新开始”的意味。

note.en: The first group shares the cedere root; the second is about verbs that also mean continuing or advancing.
note.cn: 第一组共享 cedere 词根，第二组看同样表示“继续”或“推进”的动词。

entries.definition: to come before. It uses prae- 'before' + cedere.
entries.definitionCN: 在……之前。它用 prae-“在前”+ cedere。

entries.definition: to come after; to achieve a goal. It is sub- 'under, next' + cedere.
entries.definitionCN: 随后；成功。它是 sub-“在其后”+ cedere。

entries.definition: a set of steps for doing something. It is proceed plus -ure.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的步骤。它是 proceed 加 -ure。

entries.definition: to keep doing something without stopping. It stresses duration, not direction.
entries.definitionCN: 不停顿地做下去。它强调持续，而非方向。

entries.definition: to move forward or make progress. It is closer to the physical sense of proceed.
entries.definitionCN: 向前移动或取得进展。它更接近 proceed 的物理义。

entries.definition: to develop toward a better state. It stresses improvement, not sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 朝更好状态发展。它强调改善，而非次序。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin cedere 'go', the pro- 'forward' prefix, the proceed/precede/succeed trio, and the legal use proceed against.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 cedere“走”、前缀 pro-“向前”、proceed/precede/succeed 三词，以及法律用法 proceed against。

normal.en: Cedere means 'go' and pro- means 'forward': proceed is to go forward.
normal.cn: cedere 意为“走”，pro- 意为“向前”：proceed 就是向前走。

normal.en: Precede is prae- plus cedere, 'go before'; succeed is sub- plus cedere, 'go next'. The prefix sets the position.
normal.cn: precede 是 prae- 加 cedere，“走在前面”；succeed 是 sub- 加 cedere，“接着走”。前缀定位置。

normal.en: To proceed assumes a pause: something stopped and now resumes. It is motion after a gap.
normal.cn: proceed 假定有停顿：某物停下，现在重启。它是间隙之后的运动。

normal.en: In meetings, proceed is a procedural gate: one item closes, the next opens.
normal.cn: 会议中，proceed 是程序关口：一项关闭，下一项开启。

normal.en: To proceed against someone is to start the legal machinery walking.
normal.cn: proceed against 某人，就是让法律机器开始行走。

abstract.en: Forward is both a direction and a value: progress borrows its authority from the geometry of motion.
abstract.cn: 向前既是方向也是价值：进步从运动的几何学借来权威。

abstract.en: Every procedure is a path made repeatable, so that anyone can walk it without knowing the ground.
abstract.cn: 每一种程序都是被做成可重复的路径，好让任何人都能走而不必认识地形。

abstract.en: Permission to proceed is permission to let time continue; a meeting pauses the world and then releases it.
abstract.cn: 允许 proceed，就是允许时间继续；会议暂停世界，再把它放行。

examples.en: Please proceed with your report.
examples.cn: 请继续你的报告。

examples.en: We proceeded to the next item on the agenda.
examples.cn: 我们进入议程的下一项。

examples.en: The firm proceeded against the contractor for breach of contract.
examples.cn: 公司以违约为由起诉承包商。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑若细的”——扑过去，像细线一样一路向前 → proceed 前进、继续进行

root: 拉丁语 procedere“向前走”，由 pro-“向前”+ cedere“走”构成；同族有 cede、precede、succeed、exceed。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of proceed, all one walk. The walk can resume after a break, advance in space, start a task, follow a procedure, enter the next agenda item, or enter a courtroom.
sensesIntro.cn: proceed 的九个义项，都是同一场行走。这场行走可以在休息后重启、在空间中前进、开始一项任务、遵循程序、进入下一议题，或进入法庭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: putting one foot in front of the other along a path.
core.cn: 核心意象：沿一条路一步步向前。

branches.en: RESUME: motion restarts after a pause, or an event is allowed to continue.
branches.cn: 重启：停顿后重新运动，或事件被允许继续。

branches.en: ADVANCE: physical forward movement becomes measurable progress.
branches.cn: 推进：物理的向前运动变成可测量的进展。

branches.en: NEXT STEP: the walk becomes a sequence of tasks or agenda items.
branches.cn: 下一步：行走变成任务或议程的序列。

branches.en: PROCEDURE: the path is scripted into repeatable steps.
branches.cn: 程序：路径被写成可重复的步骤。

branches.en: LAW AND SOURCE: proceed against starts legal machinery; the archaic sense comes forth from a source.
branches.cn: 法律与来源：proceed against 启动法律机器；古义指从源头出来。

intro.en: Proceed is a Latin verb. English adds -ing, -ure, and -al, and the root cedere also builds precede, succeed, exceed, and cede.
intro.cn: proceed 是拉丁动词。英语加 -ing、-ure、-al，词根 cedere 还构成 precede、succeed、exceed、cede。

latinIntro.en: Latin procedere 'go forward' sits beside cedere 'go, yield'. The family is directional: prae- gives precede, sub- gives succeed, pro- gives proceed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 procedere“向前走”旁边是 cedere“走、让”。这个词族是有方向的：prae- 生成 precede，sub- 生成 succeed，pro- 生成 proceed。

definition_zh: 过程；程序；流程；工序；（法律）程序；（计算机）进程；加工处理
definition_en: a series of actions or changes that leads to a result, or to handle something through such a series
core_image: 一条流水线：原料从一端进入，经过一道道工序，从另一端出来成品
scene: 面包房里，面团要经过发酵、整形、烘烤。Fermenting, shaping and baking take four hours, and that process turns dough into something a shop can sell.
sceneCN: 这里 process 是「流程、工序」（第 1 个义项：为达到结果而进行的一系列动作）；句意：发酵、整形、烘烤要花四小时，这个流程把面团变成店里能卖的成品。图中可辨识物件：面团、发酵箱、整形台、烤炉、出炉的面包。

pos.zh: 过程；程序；流程；工序；（计算机）进程
加工；处理（数据、材料等）

senses.title: A series of actions toward a result
senses.definition: a set of actions taken in order to achieve a result
senses.definitionCN: 为达到结果而按序采取的一组动作
senses.example: The hiring process takes three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 招聘流程需要三周。
senses.why: Latin processus is 'a going forward', from procedere. A process is a path with stages: it treats time as a route to be walked.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 processus 是“向前推进”，来自 procedere。process 是一条有阶段的路：它把时间当作要走完的路线。

senses.title: A natural series of changes
senses.definition: a course of natural changes that cannot be stopped
senses.definitionCN: 无法阻止的自然变化历程
senses.example: The process of decay begins at once.
senses.exampleCN: 腐烂过程立刻开始。
senses.why: Nature supplies the purest version: growth, erosion, decay. The word describes what happens by itself, without a planner.
senses.whyCN: 自然提供最纯粹的版本：生长、侵蚀、腐烂。这个词描述自行发生、没有规划者的事。

senses.title: A manufacturing procedure
senses.definition: the set of steps by which a product is made
senses.definitionCN: 制造产品所经的一组步骤
senses.example: The new process cuts production time in half.
senses.exampleCN: 新工序把生产时间缩短一半。
senses.why: Industry systematizes the path: each step has an input, an operation, and an output. Process becomes an engineered noun, and process engineering is born.
senses.whyCN: 工业把路径系统化：每一步都有输入、操作与输出。process 成了被工程化的名词，于是有了 process engineering。

senses.title: The legal course of proceedings
senses.definition: the formal steps required by law before a decision is valid
senses.definitionCN: 决定生效前法律要求的正式步骤
senses.example: The court must follow due process.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭必须遵循正当程序。
senses.why: Due process turns the path into a guarantee: the steps are not optional, and skipping one invalidates the result. Procedure and process converge here.
senses.whyCN: 正当程序把路径变成保障：步骤不可省略，跳过一步就使结果无效。procedure 与 process 在此汇合。

senses.title: A running program (computing)
senses.definition: an instance of a program running on a computer
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中正在运行的程序实例
senses.example: The process uses most of the memory.
senses.exampleCN: 这个进程占用了大部分内存。
senses.why: An operating system schedules tasks as a series of steps. Each running instance is a process, a path being walked by the machine.
senses.whyCN: 操作系统把任务安排成一系列步骤。每个运行实例就是一个 process，一条机器正在走的路径。

senses.title: To handle by a procedure
senses.definition: to deal with information or a request according to a set method
senses.definitionCN: 按既定方法处理信息或请求
senses.example: The computer processes thousands of forms a day.
senses.exampleCN: 计算机每天处理数千份表格。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into action: to put something through the process. What is processed has entered the line and will come out changed.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成动作：把某物送进流程。被 processed 的东西已进入流水线，出来时会变样。

senses.title: To treat food or material
senses.definition: to change a raw material by physical or chemical treatment
senses.definitionCN: 通过物理或化学处理改变原料
senses.example: The factory processes milk into cheese.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂把牛奶加工成奶酪。
senses.why: Food processing is the clearest case: the input is real, the output is real, and the stages are visible. The word carries a neutral tone, though 'processed food' can sound negative.
senses.whyCN: 食品加工是最清楚的例子：输入真实，输出真实，阶段可见。这个词语气中性，尽管 processed food 听起来可能负面。

senses.title: To move in a procession (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, to walk in an ordered group
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：按队列行走
senses.example: The choir processed down the aisle.
senses.exampleCN: 唱诗班列队走过通道。
senses.why: This archaic verb keeps the literal Latin walk. The noun procession is its surviving relative, still used for ceremonial lines of people.
senses.whyCN: 这个古义动词保留拉丁语字面的“走”。名词 procession 是它存活的亲戚，仍指礼仪性的人列。

senses.title: A bony projection (anatomy)
senses.definition: a natural outgrowth or prominence on a bone or organ
senses.definitionCN: 骨或器官上的自然突出部分
senses.example: The mastoid process lies behind the ear.
senses.exampleCN: 乳突位于耳后。
senses.why: Anatomy names protrusions 'processes' because they 'go forward' from the body of the bone. The Latin motion word becomes a shape word.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学把突出部分称作 process，因为它们从骨体“向前伸出”。拉丁运动词变成了形状词。

intro.en: Process began as 'a going forward'. Latin processus comes from procedere, 'to advance', and English first used it for the course of events, then for industrial and legal sequences, and finally for running programs.
intro.cn: process 最初意为“向前推进”。拉丁语 processus 来自 procedere“前进”，英语先用它指事件进程，再指工业与法律序列，最后指运行中的程序。

items.en: First recorded as 'the fact of being carried on; a course of events'.
items.cn: 最早记录为“被推进的事实；事件的进程”。

items.en: From Latin processus 'a going forward, advance, progress', from procedere 'go forward'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 processus“前进、推进、进展”，源出 procedere“向前走”。

items.en: procedere = pro- 'forward' + cedere 'go'. The same verb gives proceed and procedure.
items.cn: procedere = pro-“向前”+ cedere“走”。同一动词生成 proceed 与 procedure。

items.en: The modern sense 'a continuous series of actions or changes' becomes established.
items.cn: 现代义“连续的动作或变化序列”确立。

items.en: Industrial use gives process engineering and manufacturing process.
items.cn: 工业用法产生 process engineering 与 manufacturing process。

items.en: Computing adopts the word for a running program, the newest link in the same chain.
items.cn: 计算机在 1960 年代采用这个词指运行程序，是同一链条上最新的一环。

note.en: The first group shares the cedere/procedere root; the second is about nouns that also mean a series of steps.
note.cn: 第一组共享 cedere/procedere 词根，第二组看同样表示“一系列步骤”的名词。

entries.definition: to go forward; the verb behind process.
entries.definitionCN: 向前走；process 背后的动词。

entries.definition: a prescribed set of steps. It stresses the rule, not the evolution.
entries.definitionCN: 规定的步骤。它强调规则，而非演化。

entries.definition: an ordered line of people moving. It keeps the literal walking sense.
entries.definitionCN: 有序行进的人列。它保留字面的行走义。

entries.definition: an official way of doing something. It is a process with authority behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的官方方式。它是有权威支撑的 process。

entries.definition: a planned way of doing something. It stresses design, not sequence in time.
entries.definitionCN: 有计划的做事方式。它强调设计，而非时间序列。

entries.definition: the way something develops over time. It is broader and less technical than process.
entries.definitionCN: 某物随时间发展的方式。它比 process 更宽、更少技术性。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin procedere 'go forward', the proceed/procedure/process family, due process, and the computing sense.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 procedere“向前走”、proceed/procedure/process 词族、正当程序，以及计算机义。

normal.en: Processus means 'a going forward'. A process is a path with stages, walked until something comes out.
normal.cn: processus 意为“向前推进”。process 是一条有阶段的路，走到某物出来为止。

normal.en: The verb behind it is proceed: pro- 'forward' plus cedere 'go'. Process is the noun of that walk.
normal.cn: 它背后的动词是 proceed：pro-“向前”加 cedere“走”。process 是那场行走的名词。

normal.en: Procedure is a process with rules attached: the same steps, now mandatory.
normal.cn: procedure 是附上规则的 process：同样的步骤，现在成了必须。

normal.en: Due process means the steps cannot be skipped; skipping one invalidates the result.
normal.cn: 正当程序意味着步骤不可跳过；跳过一步，结果就无效。

normal.en: In computing, a process is a program mid-walk: the machine is following its steps right now.
normal.cn: 计算机中，process 是走到一半的程序：机器正在执行它的步骤。

abstract.en: A process converts time into shape: what was merely passing becomes a route with stages.
abstract.cn: 过程把时间变成形状：原本只是流逝的东西，成了有阶段的路线。

abstract.en: Calling something a process can hide responsibility: nobody did it, it just went through its steps.
abstract.cn: 把某事称作 process 可以隐藏责任：没人做的，它只是走完了步骤。

abstract.en: Nature and factory share the word because both produce an output by ordered change.
abstract.cn: 自然与工厂共享这个词，因为两者都通过有序变化产出结果。

examples.en: Learning a language is a gradual process.
examples.cn: 学语言是一个渐进的过程。

examples.en: The application process is now fully online.
examples.cn: 申请流程现已完全在线。

examples.en: The plant processes raw cocoa into chocolate.
examples.cn: 工厂把生可可加工成巧克力。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑若塞斯”——扑过去，像塞子一样一环环推进 → process 过程、流程

root: 拉丁语 processus“前进、推进”，源出 procedere“向前走”= pro-“向前”+ cedere“走”；同族有 proceed、procedure、procession。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of process, one path in different costumes. The path can be natural (decay), industrial (a production line), legal (due process), digital (a running program), or even anatomical (a bony projection).
sensesIntro.cn: process 的九个义项，是同一条路的不同装扮。这条路可以是自然的（腐烂）、工业的（生产线）、法律的（正当程序）、数字的（运行程序），甚至解剖的（骨突起）。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a route with stages, from input to output.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条有阶段的路，从输入到输出。

branches.en: COURSE: ordered change, whether planned or natural.
branches.cn: 历程：有序变化，无论有计划还是自然发生。

branches.en: MAKING: raw material enters a line and comes out changed.
branches.cn: 制造：原料进入流水线，出来时已变样。

branches.en: LAW: due process makes the steps mandatory and the result valid.
branches.cn: 法律：正当程序使步骤成为必须，使结果有效。

branches.en: COMPUTING: the path becomes a running program, and the verb means to put data through it.
branches.cn: 计算机：路径变成运行中的程序，动词意为让数据走一遍。

branches.en: SHAPE: the archaic walk survives in procession, while anatomy names protrusions 'processes'.
branches.cn: 形状：古义的行走存于 procession，解剖学则把突起称作 process。

intro.en: Process is noun and verb. English adds -ing, -or, and -ed, and the same Latin verb gives proceed, procedure, and procession.
intro.cn: process 既是名词也是动词。英语加 -ing、-or、-ed，同一拉丁动词还生成 proceed、procedure、procession。

latinIntro.en: Latin processus 'advance' comes from procedere 'go forward', built on cedere 'go'. The family is about ordered motion, from law courts to factory floors.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 processus“推进”来自 procedere“向前走”，建立在 cedere“走”上。这个词族关乎有序运动，从法庭到工厂车间。

definition_en: relating to a paid occupation, or showing the skill and standards expected in one
core_image: 一件熨得笔挺的白大褂，胸口别着写有姓名的工牌
scene: 手术室里，主刀医生动作稳而快。Every step was measured and every cut was clean, and the assistant called that level of care professional.
sceneCN: 这里 professional 是「专业的、达到职业水准的」（第 3 个义项：具备职业所需的技能与规范）；句意：每一步都经过斟酌，每一刀都干净利落，助手把这种水准称为专业。图中可辨识物件：手术台、无影灯、器械盘、白大褂、工牌。

专业人员；行家；（体育）职业选手

senses.title: Relating to a profession
senses.definition: connected with a profession or its members
senses.definitionCN: 与某个职业或其成员相关
senses.example: professional bodies set entry exams.
senses.exampleCN: 行业机构设置入行考试。
senses.why: Profession comes from Latin professio, 'a public declaration'. A professional was first someone who had publicly declared a calling, which is why the word implies a recognized field.
senses.whyCN: profession 来自拉丁语 professio“公开宣告”。professional 最初指公开宣告某种志业的人，所以这个词隐含一个被承认的领域。

senses.title: Done as a paid occupation
senses.definition: engaged in for payment rather than as a hobby
senses.definitionCN: 为报酬而从事，而非作为爱好
senses.example: She is a professional musician.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一名职业音乐家。
senses.why: The 18c. sharpened the contrast with amateur: a professional is paid, an amateur is not. Money becomes the marker that separates the two.
senses.whyCN: 18 世纪强化了与 amateur 的对比：professional 拿钱，业余者不拿。金钱成了区分两者的标记。

senses.title: Competent and skillful
senses.definition: showing the skill and care expected of a trained person
senses.definitionCN: 表现出受训者应有的技能与用心
senses.example: That was a very professional repair job.
senses.exampleCN: 那次维修做得非常专业。
senses.why: Skill turns the label into a compliment: work is professional when it meets the standard a paying client would expect. The word moves from status to quality.
senses.whyCN: 技能把这个标签变成赞美：当工作达到付费客户期待的标准，它就是专业的。这个词从身份转向品质。

senses.title: A member of a profession
senses.definition: a person who works in a profession, especially a learned one
senses.definitionCN: 从事某一职业的人，尤指需要专门学识者
senses.example: The panel included doctors and other professionals.
senses.exampleCN: 专家组包括医生及其他专业人员。
senses.why: The noun names the person behind the adjective. In modern English it often covers lawyers, doctors, engineers, and accountants — fields with entry rules and codes.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名形容词背后的人。现代英语中它常涵盖律师、医生、工程师、会计师——有准入规则与职业准则的领域。

senses.title: An expert in a field
senses.definition: a person with high skill in some activity
senses.definitionCN: 在某项活动中技能很高的人
senses.example: He is a professional when it comes to chess.
senses.exampleCN: 在国际象棋上他是个行家。
senses.why: The word can leave the salaried professions behind and simply mean 'someone who really knows'. This looser use turns expertise itself into the qualification.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以离开领薪的职业，只表示“真正懂行的人”。这种宽松用法把专长本身当成资格。

senses.title: A paid sports player
senses.definition: in sport, a player who is paid to compete
senses.definitionCN: 体育中受薪参赛的选手
senses.example: He turned professional at nineteen.
senses.exampleCN: 他十九岁转为职业选手。
senses.why: Sport copied the paid/amateur divide. Turning professional means crossing a line: from playing for love to playing for a living, with different rules and stakes.
senses.whyCN: 体育复制了“受薪／业余”的分界。转为职业，意味着跨过一条线：从为热爱而赛，到为生计而赛，规则与利害都不同。

senses.title: Conforming to professional standards
senses.definition: behaving with the ethics and manners of a profession
senses.definitionCN: 以某职业的伦理与礼节行事
senses.example: Her response was calm and professional.
senses.exampleCN: 她的回应冷静而专业。
senses.why: Conduct is judged, not skill. The word can praise someone who keeps confidences and meets deadlines, even when the task is routine.
senses.whyCN: 这里被评判的是行为，不是技能。即使任务平常，这个词也能赞美守密、守时的人。

senses.title: Of high quality, informally
senses.definition: in informal use, well-made or impressive
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法：做得好的、像样的
senses.example: They did a professional job on the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把花园弄得相当像样。
senses.why: The compliment has spread beyond occupations: anything done with care can look professional. The word now sells quality as much as status.
senses.whyCN: 这种赞美已超出职业范围：任何用心做成的事都可能显得 professional。这个词现在既卖身份，也卖品质。

senses.title: A euphemism for a sex worker (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, a euphemism for a prostitute
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：对妓女的委婉说法
senses.example: The old novel refers to her as a professional.
senses.exampleCN: 那部旧小说用 professional 指称她。
senses.why: The 'paid occupation' sense sits close to a taboo, so the euphemism was available. Modern usage avoids it because the main sense has become too respectable to carry the hint.
senses.whyCN: “受薪职业”义接近禁忌，因此这个委婉说法曾可用。现代用法避开它，因为主要义已太体面，承载不了这层暗示。

intro.en: Professional is built on profession, and profession began as a public declaration. Latin profiteri means 'declare openly', from pro- 'forth' plus fateri 'to confess'. A professional is, etymologically, someone who has declared what they do.
intro.cn: professional 建立在 profession 上，而 profession 始于“公开宣告”。拉丁语 profiteri 意为“公开宣称”，由 pro-“向前、出来”加 fateri“承认”构成。从词源看，professional 就是公开宣告自己以何为业的人。

items.en: First recorded as an adjective meaning 'of or belonging to a profession'.
items.cn: 最早记录为形容词，义为“属于某一职业的”。

items.en: profession (late 14c.) comes from Latin professionem, 'a public declaration', from profiteri 'declare openly'.
items.cn: profession（14 世纪末）来自拉丁语 professionem“公开宣告”，源出 profiteri“公开宣称”。

items.en: profiteri = pro- 'forth, publicly' + fateri 'to confess, admit'. The root fateri also gives confession and fate in related senses.
items.cn: profiteri = pro-“向外、公开”+ fateri“承认、告白”。词根 fateri 还生成 confession 等相关词。

items.en: The sense 'engaged in a profession as a paid calling' is recorded.
items.cn: “以某职业为受薪志业”的义项被记录。

items.en: The noun professional appears for a person who makes a living by a profession.
items.cn: 名词 professional 出现，指以某职业谋生的人。

items.en: Modern English extends the adjective from occupations to quality and conduct: professional advice, professional standards, a professional job.
items.cn: 现代英语把形容词从职业扩展到品质与行为：professional advice、professional standards、a professional job。

note.en: The first group shares the profession/profiteri stem; the second is about words that also mean skilled or paid.
note.cn: 第一组共享 profession/profiteri 词干，第二组看同样表示“有技能”或“受薪”的词。

entries.definition: a paid occupation requiring training. It is the noun behind professional.
entries.definitionCN: 需要训练的受薪职业。它是 professional 背后的名词。

entries.definition: the standards and conduct of a profession.
entries.definitionCN: 职业标准与职业精神。

entries.definition: a university teacher, literally one who professes a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 大学教授，字面“宣称某学科者”。

entries.definition: a person with special knowledge. It stresses knowledge, not pay or code.
entries.definitionCN: 有专门知识的人。它强调知识，而非报酬或准则。

entries.definition: having trained ability. It says nothing about a profession or payment.
entries.definitionCN: 受过训练、有能力。它不涉及职业或报酬。

entries.definition: relating to a job. It is neutral and technical, unlike the status-laden professional.
entries.definitionCN: 与工作相关的。它中性、技术性，不像 professional 带身份色彩。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin profiteri 'declare openly', the paid/amateur divide, the professional/professor family, and the modern quality sense.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 profiteri“公开宣称”、受薪／业余之分、professional/professor 词族，以及现代品质义。

normal.en: Latin profiteri means 'declare openly': a professional has publicly declared what they do.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 profiteri 意为“公开宣称”：professional 已公开宣告自己以何为业。

normal.en: The 18c. made money the test: professionals are paid, amateurs are not.
normal.cn: 18 世纪以金钱为标准：professional 受薪，业余者不受薪。

normal.en: Professor and professional share the root: both publicly profess a field.
normal.cn: professor 与 professional 共享词根：两者都公开宣称某个领域。

normal.en: The word has moved from status to quality: a professional job is simply a job done to a high standard.
normal.cn: 这个词从身份滑向品质：a professional job 就是做得高标准的工作。

normal.en: In sport, turning professional means crossing from playing for love to playing for a living.
normal.cn: 体育中，转为职业意味着从为热爱而赛，跨到为生计而赛。

abstract.en: A profession is a public promise: the declaration is what binds the practitioner to a code.
abstract.cn: 职业是一份公开承诺：宣告把从业者绑定到一套准则上。

abstract.en: Professionalism is a form of trust infrastructure: strangers can rely on you because a field vouches for you.
abstract.cn: 专业精神是一种信任基础设施：陌生人能依赖你，因为一个领域为你背书。

abstract.en: When the word praises quality rather than occupation, it shows how deeply work and identity are fused in modern life.
abstract.cn: 当这个词赞美品质而非职业时，它显示出工作与身份在现代生活中融合得有多深。

examples.en: You should seek professional advice before investing.
examples.cn: 投资前你应当寻求专业建议。

examples.en: She handled the complaint in a professional manner.
examples.cn: 她以专业的方式处理了这起投诉。

examples.en: He became a professional football player at twenty.
examples.cn: 他二十岁时成为职业足球运动员。

root: 由 profession + -al 构成；profession 来自拉丁语 professio“公开宣告”，源出 profiteri“公开宣称”= pro-“向外”+ fateri“承认”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of professional, all built on a public declaration. The declaration can name an occupation, mark payment, certify skill, impose conduct, or simply advertise quality.
sensesIntro.cn: professional 的九个义项都建立在一次公开宣告上。这次宣告可以命名职业、标记受薪、证明技能、施加行为准则，或仅仅为品质作广告。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a public declaration that binds a person to a standard.
core.cn: 核心意象：一次公开宣告，把人绑定到某个标准上。

branches.en: FIELD: a recognized occupation and the people who belong to it.
branches.cn: 领域：被承认的职业及其成员。

branches.en: PAY: the paid/amateur line, in work and in sport.
branches.cn: 报酬：工作与体育中的受薪／业余分界。

branches.en: SKILL: training shows as competence, and competence can stand alone as expertise.
branches.cn: 技能：训练表现为胜任，胜任又可单独成为专长。

branches.en: ETHICS: conduct is judged by the standards of the field.
branches.cn: 伦理：行为按该领域的标准被评判。

branches.en: EXTENSIONS: informal praise of quality, and an archaic euphemism that the main sense has outgrown.
branches.cn: 延伸：对品质的非正式赞美，以及主要义已使其不再适用的旧委婉语。

intro.en: Professional is profession plus -al. English adds -ly, -ism, -ize, and the negative un-, while the Latin fateri also gives confess and confession.
intro.cn: professional 是 profession 加 -al。英语加 -ly、-ism、-ize 与否定 un-，拉丁语 fateri 还生成 confess 与 confession。

latinIntro.en: Latin professio 'public declaration' and profiteri 'declare openly' combine pro- 'forth' with fateri 'admit'. The family is about public avowal, not merely employment.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 professio“公开宣告”与 profiteri“公开宣称”把 pro-“向外”与 fateri“承认”结合。这个词族关乎公开表态，而不只是就业。

definition_zh: 禁止；阻止；使不可能；（法律）禁止某人做某事
definition_en: to forbid something by law or rule, or to make it impossible
core_image: 一只手横在门前，掌心朝外，把来人挡回去
scene: 博物馆入口挂着一块牌子。The sign at the entrance says that the rules prohibit flash photography, and the guard raises a hand whenever a camera comes up.
sceneCN: 这里 prohibit 是「禁止」（第 1 个义项：以规则明令不许做某事）；句意：入口的牌子写着规定禁止使用闪光灯，保安一看到有人举相机就抬手示意。图中可辨识物件：禁止标识、相机、闪光灯、保安的手、展厅入口。

pos.zh: 禁止；阻止；使不可能

derivatives.zh: 禁止的；（价格）高得使人却步的

senses.title: Forbid by law or rule
senses.definition: to state officially that something must not be done
senses.definitionCN: 官方规定某事不得做
senses.example: The law prohibits smoking indoors.
senses.exampleCN: 法律禁止室内吸烟。
senses.why: Latin prohibere means 'hold back'. The prefix pro- pushes away, and habere holds: the rule puts a hand out and holds the thing back from happening.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 prohibere 意为“挡住”。前缀 pro- 向外推，habere 是持握：规则伸出一只手，把此事挡在外面。

senses.title: Prevent or make impossible
senses.definition: to make something impossible in practice
senses.definitionCN: 使某事在实践中不可能
senses.example: The high cost prohibits most families from buying.
senses.exampleCN: 高昂的成本使多数家庭无法购买。
senses.why: The same holding-back can be economic rather than legal: price acts like a gate. Prohibitive costs prohibit without any statute.
senses.whyCN: 同一种“挡住”可以是经济的而非法律的：价格像一道门。 prohibitive 的成本无需法规就禁止了购买。

senses.title: Forbid a person from doing
senses.definition: to bar a specific person from an action
senses.definitionCN: 禁止特定的人采取某行动
senses.example: The court prohibited him from contacting her.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭禁止他联系她。
senses.why: When the object is a person, the rule targets an agent rather than an act. The structure prohibit someone from doing marks the boundary drawn around that person.
senses.whyCN: 当对象是人时，规则瞄准行动者而非行为本身。prohibit someone from doing 的结构，标记围绕此人画下的边界。

senses.title: An official ban
senses.definition: to ban something officially, often by authority
senses.definitionCN: 由权威正式取缔某物
senses.example: The city prohibited the sale of fireworks.
senses.exampleCN: 该市禁止销售烟花爆竹。
senses.why: A ban is the institutional form of the hand at the door. Prohibition is the noun, and it can name a whole historical policy, as in the American Prohibition.
senses.whyCN: 禁令是“门口那只手”的制度形式。prohibition 是名词，可以命名一整段历史政策，如美国禁酒令。

senses.title: Of a sign or notice: forbid entry or use
senses.definition: of a sign or instruction, to forbid an action or access
senses.definitionCN: 标识或指示禁止某行为或进入
senses.example: The sign prohibits entry without a badge.
senses.exampleCN: 标牌禁止无证进入。
senses.why: Public space is regulated by visible marks. The verb turns a printed symbol into a rule, and the sign becomes the hand made permanent.
senses.whyCN: 公共空间由可见标记管理。动词把印刷符号变成规则，标牌成了被永久化的那只手。

senses.title: Hinder or prevent (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, to hinder or stand in the way of
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：妨碍或挡路
senses.example: Bad weather prohibited our advance.
senses.exampleCN: 恶劣天气阻碍了我们前进。
senses.why: This is the broadest layer: anything that holds you back prohibits you. Modern English narrows the word to rules and practical impossibility.
senses.whyCN: 这是最宽的一层：任何挡住你的东西都 prohibit 你。现代英语把这个词收窄到规则与实际不可能。

senses.title: Restrain by legal writ
senses.definition: in law, to restrain an action by authority
senses.definitionCN: 法律中以权威限制某行为
senses.example: The injunction prohibits further construction.
senses.exampleCN: 禁令限制继续施工。
senses.why: Courts issue orders that function as verbal gates. The legal sense specializes the holding-back into a formal instrument with penalties attached.
senses.whyCN: 法院发布命令，功能如同语言的门。法律义把“挡住”专门化为附有惩罚的正式工具。

senses.title: Forbid access
senses.definition: to bar entry to a place
senses.definitionCN: 不许进入某地
senses.example: The area is prohibited to civilians.
senses.exampleCN: 该区域禁止平民进入。
senses.why: Access control is the most physical version: a fence, a guard, a sign. The verb names the rule that the barrier enforces.
senses.whyCN: 出入控制是最物理的版本：围栏、警卫、标牌。动词命名屏障所执行的规则。

intro.en: Prohibit is a holding-back word. Latin prohibere joins pro- 'away' to habere 'hold': to hold something away from you, and therefore to forbid it.
intro.cn: prohibit 是一个“挡住”的词。拉丁语 prohibere 把 pro-“向外”与 habere“持握”结合：把某物挡在你之外，因此就是禁止它。

items.en: First recorded as 'forbid, prevent', borrowed from Latin prohibitus.
items.cn: 最早记录为“禁止、阻止”，借自拉丁语 prohibitus。

items.en: prohibitus is the past participle of prohibere 'hold back, keep off, prevent, forbid' = pro- 'away, forth' + habere 'to hold'.
items.cn: prohibitus 是 prohibere 的过去分词，后者意为“挡住、隔开、阻止、禁止”= pro-“向外”+ habere“持握”。

items.en: habere also gives habit, exhibit, inhibit, and ability. The family is about holding, and pro- turns holding into holding away.
items.cn: habere 还生成 habit、exhibit、inhibit、ability。这个词族关乎持握，而 pro- 把“持握”变成“挡开”。

items.en: The noun prohibition and the adjective prohibitive develop, the latter also taking the sense 'so costly as to prevent'.
items.cn: 名词 prohibition 与形容词 prohibitive 发展出来，后者还取得“贵到使人却步”的义。

items.en: Modern English uses prohibit for legal bans, signs, and practical impossibility, keeping the image of a hand held out.
items.cn: 现代英语用 prohibit 指法律禁令、标识与实际不可能，保留“伸出手挡住”的意象。

note.en: The first group shares the habere root; the second is about verbs that also mean forbidding or preventing.
note.cn: 第一组共享 habere 词根，第二组看同样表示“禁止”或“阻止”的动词。

entries.definition: to restrain or slow down. It uses in- 'in' + habere, holding in.
entries.definitionCN: 抑制；阻碍。它用 in-“在内”+ habere，持握在内。

entries.definition: to show publicly. It is ex- 'out' + habere, holding out.
entries.definitionCN: 公开展示。它是 ex-“向外”+ habere，持出在外。

entries.definition: an official ban, or the historical US ban on alcohol.
entries.definitionCN: 官方禁令；美国禁酒令。

entries.definition: to order someone not to do something. It is broader and more personal than prohibit.
entries.definitionCN: 命令某人不要做。它比 prohibit 更宽、更对人。

entries.definition: to forbid something officially, often by public authority. It is the plain word behind prohibition.
entries.definitionCN: 官方禁止，常由公共权威发布。它是 prohibition 背后的平实词。

entries.definition: to stop something from happening. It covers both rules and practical obstacles.
entries.definitionCN: 阻止某事发生。它涵盖规则与实际障碍。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin habere 'hold' with pro- 'away', the inhibit/exhibit family, the sign use, and prohibitive cost.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 habere“持握”加 pro-“向外”、inhibit/exhibit 词族、标识用法，以及 prohibitive cost。

normal.en: Habere means 'hold'; pro- means 'away'. Prohibit is to hold something away from you: a hand at the door.
normal.cn: habere 意为“持握”；pro- 意为“向外”。prohibit 就是把东西挡在你之外：门口的一只手。

normal.en: Inhibit holds in, exhibit holds out, prohibit holds away: the prefix tells you the direction.
normal.cn: inhibit 向内持，exhibit 向外持，prohibit 挡开：前缀告诉你方向。

normal.en: A prohibition sign is the hand made permanent: the rule stays at the door even when no guard is there.
normal.cn: 禁止标识是被永久化的那只手：即使没有警卫，规则仍守在门口。

normal.en: Prohibitive costs prohibit without a law: price acts as a gate.
normal.cn: prohibitive 的成本无需法律就禁止：价格就是门。

normal.en: The word targets both acts and people: you prohibit smoking, and you prohibit someone from smoking.
normal.cn: 这个词既针对行为也针对人：prohibit smoking，也 prohibit someone from smoking。

abstract.en: Every prohibition draws a boundary, and every boundary creates a category of the forbidden.
abstract.cn: 每一项禁令都画出一条边界，每条边界都造出“被禁止者”这一类别。

abstract.en: Forbidding is cheaper than preventing: a rule costs words, a wall costs stone.
abstract.cn: 禁止比阻止便宜：规则花的是话，墙花的是石头。

abstract.en: The same verb covers law and economics, which shows that constraint has many currencies.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词覆盖法律与经济，说明约束有多种货币。

examples.en: Smoking is prohibited in all public buildings.
examples.cn: 所有公共建筑内禁止吸烟。

examples.en: The high price prohibits many students from applying.
examples.cn: 高昂的价格使许多学生无法申请。

examples.en: The court prohibited the company from selling the drug.
examples.cn: 法庭禁止该公司销售这种药物。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of prohibit, all one gesture: holding something away. The hand can be a law, a sign, a court order, a price, or a fence.
sensesIntro.cn: prohibit 的八个义项，都是同一个手势：把某物挡在外面。这只手可以是法律、标识、法院命令、价格或围栏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand held out to keep something away.
core.cn: 核心意象：伸出一只手，把某物挡在外面。

branches.en: RULE: laws, bans, and signs state what must not be done.
branches.cn: 规则：法律、禁令与标识规定什么不得做。

branches.en: PERSON AND COURT: an order can be drawn around a specific person or action.
branches.cn: 人与法庭：命令可围绕特定人或行为画界。

branches.en: ACCESS: a barrier enforces the rule at a physical threshold.

branches.en: ECONOMICS: price holds people back without any statute.

branches.en: HINDRANCE: the archaic sense covers any obstacle that holds you back.

definition_zh: 项目；工程；课题；计划；投射；凸出；预测；表现（形象）
definition_en: a planned piece of work, or to throw something forward in space, time, or imagination
core_image: 把一张纸向前抛出去，纸面在空中展开成一块可见的平面
scene: 会议室里，团队把目标、时间线、负责人写在墙上。The whole project is pinned to the wall, with its goals, its timeline and the name of the person who owns each part.
sceneCN: 这里 project 是「项目、工程」（第 1 个义项：为达成目标而规划的一整块工作）；句意：整个项目都贴在墙上，写着目标、时间线，以及每一部分的负责人。图中可辨识物件：项目看板、便利贴、时间线、负责人照片、马克笔。

pos.zh: 项目；工程；课题；计划
投射；凸出；预测；表现（形象）；使（影像）成像

senses.title: A planned piece of work
senses.definition: a planned undertaking with a goal, a timetable, and resources
senses.definitionCN: 有计划、有目标、有时间与资源的任务
senses.example: The bridge project will take five years.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥的工程要五年。
senses.why: Latin proiectum is 'something thrown forward'. A project is a plan thrown ahead of you, a future state you have already sketched.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 proiectum 是“被抛向前之物”。project 是被投到你前方的计划，一幅你已勾画出的未来图景。

senses.title: A research or study topic
senses.definition: a specific piece of research or academic work
senses.definitionCN: 一项具体的研究或学术工作
senses.example: She is working on a project about urban birds.
senses.exampleCN: 她在做一个关于城市鸟类的课题。
senses.why: Schools and labs cut knowledge into manageable pieces. Each project is a bounded task with its own question, method, and deadline.
senses.whyCN: 学校与实验室把知识切成可处理的块。每个 project 都是有界任务，有自己的问题、方法与期限。

senses.title: To estimate or forecast
senses.definition: to calculate what a quantity will be in the future
senses.definitionCN: 计算某数量在未来会是多少
senses.example: Analysts project a rise in demand.
senses.exampleCN: 分析师预计需求上升。
senses.why: Forecasting is throwing a number forward in time. The same verb that launches an object through space launches a figure into next year.
senses.whyCN: 预测是把一个数字抛向未来。同一个把物体抛过空间的动词，也把数字抛进明年。

senses.title: To throw forward physically
senses.definition: to throw or cast something forward
senses.definitionCN: 把某物向前抛
senses.example: The machine projects balls at high speed.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器高速抛出球。
senses.why: This is the literal core: iacere 'to throw' with pro- 'forward'. Every abstract sense is a metaphor built on this physical cast.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面核心：iacere“投”加 pro-“向前”。一切抽象义都建在这个物理抛掷上。

senses.title: To cast an image onto a surface
senses.definition: to cause light or an image to fall on a surface
senses.definitionCN: 使光或影像落在某个表面
senses.example: The device projects the map onto the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 设备把地图投射到墙上。
senses.why: Light is thrown forward and lands on a screen. The projector is the object that throws, and the image is what arrives.
senses.whyCN: 光被抛向前方，落在屏幕上。projector 是抛掷之物，影像则是到达之物。

senses.title: To extend outward
senses.definition: of a part, to stick out beyond the main body
senses.definitionCN: 某部分超出主体向外伸
senses.example: The balcony projects over the street.
senses.exampleCN: 阳台向街道上方凸出。
senses.why: A shape that juts out is literally thrown beyond the wall. Architecture uses the word for any part that advances past its base.
senses.whyCN: 向外突出的形状，字面上被抛出了墙外。建筑学用这个词指任何越过基线的部分。

senses.title: To convey an impression
senses.definition: to communicate a quality or image to others
senses.definitionCN: 向他人传达某种品质或形象
senses.example: A good speaker projects confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 好的演讲者展现自信。
senses.why: Social presence is treated as a projection: an inner state is thrown outward so others can see it. The word implies deliberate display.
senses.whyCN: 社会在场被当作一种投射：内在状态被抛到外面，让他人看见。这个词隐含刻意的展示。

senses.title: To predict by extrapolation
senses.definition: to extend a trend or pattern into the future
senses.definitionCN: 把趋势或模式延伸到未来
senses.example: The model projects growth through 2030.
senses.exampleCN: 模型推算增长将持续到 2030 年。
senses.why: Statistics throws a line forward from known points. Projection is the noun, and it always carries the caveat that the future may not land where the line points.
senses.whyCN: 统计把一条线从已知点向前抛。projection 是名词，且总带着警告：未来未必落在线的落点。

senses.title: To protrude anatomically
senses.definition: of a body part, to stick out from the surface
senses.definitionCN: 身体某部分从表面突出
senses.example: The jaw projects forward.
senses.exampleCN: 下颌向前突出。
senses.why: Bones and features can be thrown beyond the body's outline. Anatomy uses the same spatial verb as architecture, applied to flesh.
senses.whyCN: 骨与特征可以超出身体轮廓。解剖学把与建筑相同的空间动词用于肉体。

senses.title: To map onto a plane (geometry)
senses.definition: to represent a figure on a plane by drawing lines from it
senses.definitionCN: 用射线把图形表示到平面上
senses.example: Project the sphere onto a flat map.
senses.exampleCN: 把球面投影到平面地图上。
senses.why: Geometry formalizes the light image: points are carried along rays to a surface. Map projections keep the same metaphor, with distortion as the price.
senses.whyCN: 几何学把光的意象形式化：点沿射线被带到表面。地图投影保留同一隐喻，代价是变形。

intro.en: Project is a throwing word. Latin proicere joins pro- 'forward' to iacere 'to throw'. A plan, an image, a forecast, and a balcony are all things thrown ahead of the body.
intro.cn: project 是一个抛掷词。拉丁语 proicere 把 pro-“向前”与 iacere“投”结合。计划、影像、预测与阳台，都是被抛到身体前方的东西。

items.en: The noun is first recorded as 'a plan, scheme, design'.
items.cn: 名词最早记录为“计划、方案、设计”。

items.en: From Latin proiectum 'something thrown forth', neuter past participle of proicere 'throw forward' = pro- 'forward' + iacere 'to throw'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 proiectum“被抛向前之物”，是 proicere“向前抛”的中性过去分词 = pro-“向前”+ iacere“投”。

items.en: iacere also gives eject, inject, reject, subject, and object. The family is about throwing, and the prefix sets the direction.
items.cn: iacere 还生成 eject、inject、reject、subject、object。这个词族关乎投掷，前缀定方向。

items.en: The verb appears with the sense 'to throw or cast forward'.
items.cn: 动词出现，义为“向前投掷”。

items.en: Projection extends to optics, psychology (projecting an image), and statistics (projecting a trend).
items.cn: projection 扩展到光学、心理学（投射形象）与统计学（推算趋势）。

items.en: Modern English uses project for both a planned task and the act of throwing an image, a forecast, or a shape forward.
items.cn: 现代英语用 project 既指计划任务，也指把影像、预测或形状向前抛出的动作。

note.en: The first group shares the iacere root and the -ject shape; the second is about words that also mean a plan or a forecast.
note.cn: 第一组共享 iacere 词根与 -ject 形态，第二组看同样表示“计划”或“预测”的词。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin iacere 'throw', the pro- 'forward' prefix, the reject/inject/eject family, and the optics and statistics uses.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 iacere“投”、前缀 pro-“向前”、reject/inject/eject 词族，以及光学与统计用法。

normal.en: Iacere means 'throw'; pro- means 'forward'. A project is something thrown ahead of you.
normal.cn: iacere 意为“投”；pro- 意为“向前”。project 是被抛到你前方的东西。

normal.en: Reject throws back, inject throws in, eject throws out, project throws forward: the prefix is the direction.
normal.cn: reject 掷回，inject 掷入，eject 掷出，project 掷向前：前缀就是方向。

normal.en: A projector throws light; a balcony throws itself beyond the wall; a forecast throws a number into next year.
normal.cn: 投影仪抛光；阳台把自己抛出墙外；预测把数字抛进明年。

normal.en: Project management is planning seen as a launched object: it has a target, a trajectory, and a landing date.
normal.cn: 项目管理就是把计划看作被发射的物体：它有目标、弹道与落地日期。

normal.en: Projecting confidence is throwing an inner state outward so others can catch it.
normal.cn: 展现自信，是把内在状态抛到外面，让他人接住。

abstract.en: Planning is projective: to make a project is to live in a future you have already thrown into view.
abstract.cn: 规划是投射性的：做一个项目，就是住在一个已被你抛入视野的未来里。

abstract.en: Every projection distorts: a map, a forecast, and a self-image all flatten something three-dimensional.
abstract.cn: 每一种投影都会变形：地图、预测与自我形象，都把某种立体之物压平。

abstract.en: The word ties action to imagination: what we throw forward is first an object of thought, then a thing in the world.
abstract.cn: 这个词把行动与想象绑在一起：我们抛向前方的，先是思想的对象，然后才是世界中的实物。

examples.en: The team finished the project ahead of schedule.
examples.cn: 团队提前完成了项目。

examples.en: The film was projected onto a huge screen.
examples.cn: 影片被投射到一块巨大的屏幕上。

examples.en: Sales are projected to grow by ten percent.
examples.cn: 销售额预计增长百分之十。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of project, all one throw. What is thrown can be a plan (a project), an image (a projection), a number (a forecast), a wall (a balcony), or a self (a persona).
sensesIntro.cn: project 的十个义项，都是同一次抛掷。被抛出的可以是计划（项目）、影像（投影）、数字（预测）、墙体（阳台），或自我（形象）。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something thrown forward from the body into space or time.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物从身体被抛向前方，进入空间或时间。

branches.en: PLAN: a future task sketched and thrown ahead.
branches.cn: 计划：被勾画并抛向前方的未来任务。

branches.en: CAST: physical throwing, light onto a surface, and geometric projection.
branches.cn: 投射：物理抛掷、光落表面与几何投影。

branches.en: PROTRUDE: a part thrown beyond the outline, in buildings and bodies.
branches.cn: 凸出：在建筑与身体中超出轮廓的部分。

branches.en: PERSONA: an inner state thrown outward for others to see.
branches.cn: 形象：内在状态被抛向外，供他人看见。

branches.en: FORECAST: a number or trend carried into the future.
branches.cn: 预测：被带到未来的数字或趋势。

intro.en: Project is noun and verb. English adds -ion, -or, and -ed, and the root iacere also builds reject, inject, eject, and subject.
intro.cn: project 既是名词也是动词。英语加 -ion、-or、-ed，词根 iacere 还构成 reject、inject、eject、subject。

latinIntro.en: Latin proicere 'throw forward' and its participle proiectum stand beside iacere 'throw'. The -ject family is a set of directions: re- back, in- in, e- out, pro- forward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 proicere“向前抛”及其分词 proiectum 旁边是 iacere“投”。-ject 词族是一组方向：re- 向后、in- 向内、e- 向外、pro- 向前。

definition_zh: 提升；晋升；促进；推动；推销；宣传；（棋）升变
definition_en: to move someone or something to a higher position, or to encourage its growth or acceptance
core_image: 一只手把一个人从台阶的下层托到上一层
scene: 公司年会上，经理把一位做了五年的一线员工叫到台前。The manager decided to promote her from team leader to department head after five years on the line.
sceneCN: 这里 promote 是「提升、晋升」（第 1 个义项：把某人移到更高的职位）；句意：经理决定把在一线做了五年的她从组长提升为部门主管。图中可辨识物件：舞台、晋升名单、新工牌、握手、掌声。

pos.zh: 提升；晋升；促进；推销；宣传

senses.title: Advance someone in rank
senses.definition: to move a person to a higher position or rank
senses.definitionCN: 把某人移到更高的职位或等级
senses.example: She was promoted to department head.
senses.exampleCN: 她被提升为部门主管。
senses.why: Latin promovere means 'move forward': pro- 'forward' plus movere 'to move'. A promotion moves a person up the institutional ladder.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 promovere 意为“向前移动”：pro-“向前”加 movere“移动”。晋升就是把一个人沿机构的梯子往上移。

senses.title: Encourage growth or success
senses.definition: to help something grow, develop, or succeed
senses.definitionCN: 帮助某事物成长、发展或成功
senses.example: The policy promotes small businesses.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策促进小企业。
senses.why: The object changes from a person to a process: what is promoted is made to move forward. The word becomes a general verb of support.
senses.whyCN: 对象从人变成过程：被 promote 的东西被推着向前。这个词变成泛用的支持动词。

senses.title: Advertise or publicize
senses.definition: to make a product, idea, or event known in order to sell or gain support
senses.definitionCN: 使产品、理念或活动为人所知，以销售或争取支持
senses.example: The company promotes its new phone online.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在网上推销新手机。
senses.why: Commerce borrows the ladder image: a product is moved forward in the market, pushed toward buyers. Promotion becomes the noun of marketing.
senses.whyCN: 商业借来梯子意象：产品在市场中被向前推，推向买家。promotion 于是成了营销名词。

senses.title: Move a pupil to the next grade
senses.definition: to advance a student to the next class or level
senses.definitionCN: 把学生升到下一个班级或年级
senses.example: All students were promoted to the next grade.
senses.exampleCN: 所有学生都升到了下一个年级。
senses.why: Schools use the same upward motion: a pupil moves from one level to the next. The opposite, to hold back, keeps the spatial logic.
senses.whyCN: 学校用同一个向上运动：学生从一级移到下一级。反义词“留级”保留同样的空间逻辑。

senses.title: Cause an idea or cause to advance
senses.definition: to help a cause, idea, or value become stronger or more accepted
senses.definitionCN: 帮助事业、理念或价值变得更强、更被接受
senses.example: The campaign promotes healthy eating.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动推广健康饮食。
senses.why: Public language treats values as objects that can be pushed forward. To promote peace is to give it momentum in the world.
senses.whyCN: 公共语言把价值当作可被推向前方的物体。promote peace 就是让和平在世界上获得动量。

senses.title: Advance a pawn in chess
senses.definition: in chess, to move a pawn to the last rank and replace it with a stronger piece
senses.definitionCN: 国际象棋中，把兵走到对方底线并换成更强的子
senses.example: The pawn was promoted to a queen.
senses.exampleCN: 那个兵升变为后。
senses.why: Chess gives the ladder literal form: a lowly pawn reaches the far rank and becomes a queen. The metaphor of advancement becomes a rule of the game.
senses.whyCN: 国际象棋把梯子变成字面规则：卑微的兵走到远端，变成后。“晋升”隐喻成了游戏规则。

senses.title: Move a team to a higher league
senses.definition: in sport, to move a club or player to a higher division
senses.definitionCN: 体育中把俱乐部或选手升到更高级别
senses.example: The club was promoted to the first division.
senses.exampleCN: 该俱乐部升入甲级。
senses.why: League tables rank teams by results. Promotion is the reward for finishing high, and relegation is its mirror. The word makes sport a visible ladder.
senses.whyCN: 联赛积分榜按成绩给球队排序。升级是名列前茅的奖赏，降级是它的镜像。这个词让体育成了一条可见的梯子。

senses.title: Accelerate a chemical reaction
senses.definition: in chemistry, to increase the rate of a reaction
senses.definitionCN: 化学中加快反应速率
senses.example: The catalyst promotes the reaction.
senses.exampleCN: 催化剂促进该反应。
senses.why: A catalyst moves a reaction forward without being consumed. Science uses promote for any agent that speeds a process, keeping the 'move forward' core.
senses.whyCN: 催化剂推动反应向前，自身不被消耗。科学用 promote 指任何加速过程的因素，保留“向前移动”核心。

senses.title: Push forward physically (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, to move something forward in space
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：把某物在空间中向前推
senses.example: The crowd promoted him toward the door.
senses.exampleCN: 人群把他推向门口。
senses.why: This is the literal Latin sense, now rare. Modern English keeps it mainly in the abstract ladder, but the physical push is still visible in the metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁字面义，现已罕见。现代英语主要在抽象梯子中保留它，但物理的“推”仍能在隐喻中看见。

intro.en: Promote is a forward-motion word: Latin promovere joins pro- 'forward' to movere 'to move'. English borrowed it in the late 14c. and then applied the same push to careers, causes, products, and pawns.
intro.cn: promote 是一个向前运动的词：拉丁语 promovere 把 pro-“向前”与 movere“移动”结合。英语在 14 世纪末借入，随后把同一推动用到职业、事业、产品与棋子。

items.en: First recorded with the sense 'advance, further, encourage'.
items.cn: 最早记录为“推进、促进、鼓励”。

items.en: From Latin promovere 'move forward, advance, bring forward' = pro- 'forward' + movere 'to move'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 promovere“向前移、推进、带上前”= pro-“向前”+ movere“移动”。

items.en: movere also gives move, remove, motive, emotion, and moment. The family is about motion, and pro- turns it into forward motion.
items.cn: movere 还生成 move、remove、motive、emotion、moment。这个词族关乎运动，pro- 把它变成向前运动。

items.en: The senses 'raise to a higher office' and 'help forward a cause' become established.
items.cn: “提升到更高职位”与“推动某项事业”的义项确立。

items.en: Commercial promotion appears: advertising pushes goods toward buyers.
items.cn: 商业推广义出现：广告把商品推向买家。

items.en: Modern English uses promote for careers, health, products, teams, and chemical reactions, always with the same forward push.
items.cn: 现代英语用 promote 指职业、健康、产品、球队与化学反应，始终是同一个向前推动。

note.en: The first group shares the movere root and the -mote shape; the second is about verbs that also mean raising or supporting.
note.cn: 第一组共享 movere 词根与 -mote 形态，第二组看同样表示“提升”或“支持”的动词。

entries.definition: a person who organizes or backs an event or business.

entries.definition: far away, literally 'moved back'. It is re- 'back' + movere.
entries.definitionCN: 遥远的，字面“被移开”。它是 re-“向后”+ movere。

entries.definition: to move forward or raise in rank. It overlaps promote but is less institutional.
entries.definitionCN: 向前移动或提升等级。它与 promote 重叠，但更少机构色彩。

entries.definition: to give someone confidence or help something grow. It names morale and support, not position.
entries.definitionCN: 给某人信心或助长某事。它命名士气与支持，而非职位。

entries.definition: to make something widely known. It matches the advertising sense but not the career sense.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事广为人知。它对应推销义，不对应职业义。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin movere 'move', the pro- 'forward' prefix, the promotion/promoter pair, and the chess and league uses.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 movere“移动”、前缀 pro-“向前”、promotion/promoter 这对词，以及国际象棋与联赛用法。

normal.en: Movere means 'move' and pro- means 'forward': promote is to move someone or something forward.
normal.cn: movere 意为“移动”，pro- 意为“向前”：promote 就是把某人或某物向前移。

normal.en: The same push serves a career, a cause, a product, and a pawn: all are moved up or forward.
normal.cn: 同一个推动服务职业、事业、产品与棋子：它们都被向上或向前推。

normal.en: Remote is re- plus movere, 'moved back'; promote is pro- plus movere, 'moved forward'. One prefix, two directions.
normal.cn: remote 是 re- 加 movere，“被移开”；promote 是 pro- 加 movere，“被推向前”。一个前缀，两个方向。

normal.en: In sport, promotion is the reward for finishing high, and relegation is its mirror image.
normal.cn: 体育中，升级是名列前茅的奖赏，降级是它的镜像。

normal.en: A catalyst promotes a reaction without being consumed: it pushes the process forward and stays.
normal.cn: 催化剂促进反应而自身不被消耗：它把过程推向前，并留在原地。

abstract.en: Advancement is a spatial metaphor: we imagine a career as a ladder and call each step a promotion.
abstract.cn: 晋升是一种空间隐喻：我们把职业想象成梯子，把每一级称作 promotion。

abstract.en: To promote an idea is to give it momentum in other minds, not merely to mention it.
abstract.cn: 推动一个理念，是给它在他者心智中的动量，而不只是提到它。

abstract.en: The chess pawn shows the metaphor literally: the lowest piece can become the highest by reaching the far rank.
abstract.cn: 国际象棋的兵把隐喻变成字面：最低的子只要走到远端，就能变成最高的子。

examples.en: She was promoted to senior manager last month.
examples.cn: 她上个月被提升为高级经理。

examples.en: The campaign promotes recycling in schools.
examples.cn: 这场运动在学校推广回收。

examples.en: Exercise promotes good health at every age.
examples.cn: 运动在各年龄段都促进健康。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑若谋特”——扑过去谋划，把特出的人往上推 → promote 提升、促进

root: 拉丁语 promovere“向前移”，由 pro-“向前”+ movere“移动”构成；同族有 move、remove、motive、emotion。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of promote, all the same forward push. The push can raise a person, grow a cause, sell a product, advance a pupil, crown a pawn, or speed a reaction.
sensesIntro.cn: promote 的九个义项，都是同一个向前推动。这个推可以提升一个人、壮大一项事业、卖出产品、让学生升级、让兵升变，或加速反应。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pushing a person or thing forward and upward.
core.cn: 核心意象：把人或物向前、向上推。

branches.en: RANK: a person, pupil, or team moves to a higher level.
branches.cn: 等级：人、学生或球队移到更高层。

branches.en: GROWTH: causes and values are given momentum in the world.
branches.cn: 成长：事业与价值在世界中获得动量。

branches.en: MARKET: goods are pushed toward buyers through publicity.
branches.cn: 市场：商品通过宣传被推向买家。

branches.en: GAME: a pawn reaches the far rank and becomes a stronger piece.
branches.cn: 游戏：兵走到远端，变成更强的子。

branches.en: PROCESS: chemistry speeds a reaction, and the archaic sense keeps the physical push.
branches.cn: 过程：化学加速反应，古义保留物理推动。

intro.en: Promote is a Latin verb. English adds -ion, -er, and -ional, and the root movere also builds move, remove, motive, and emotion.
intro.cn: promote 是拉丁动词。英语加 -ion、-er、-ional，词根 movere 还构成 move、remove、motive、emotion。

latinIntro.en: Latin promovere 'move forward' joins pro- 'forward' to movere 'move'. The same movere appears in remote (moved back), remove, and motive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 promovere“向前移”把 pro-“向前”与 movere“移动”结合。同一个 movere 出现在 remote（移开）、remove、motive。

items.meaningCN: 晋升；促销（-ion 构成名词）

relating to advertising
